  • Cryptocurrency prices are bouncing back, with Bitcoin (BTC), XRP and Shiba Inu (SHIB) all in the green after the surprising announcement that Jensen Huang has been reappointed as chief executive officer of Nvidia.
  • The sudden leadership reversal comes as tech stocks bounce back following the sharp market sell-off that has also affected major crypto assets.
  • It has been revealed that nvidia made a major announcement on Monday, Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cryptocurrency prices are bouncing back, with Bitcoin (BTC), XRP and Shiba Inu (SHIB) all in the green after the surprising announcement that Jensen Huang has been reappointed as chief executive officer of Nvidia.

The sudden leadership reversal comes as tech stocks bounce back following the sharp market sell-off that has also affected major crypto assets.

It has been revealed that nvidia made a major announcement on Monday, Nov. 23, stating that its board of directors had unanimously approved Huang's reappointment as the company’s president, CEO, and a board director, effective immediately.

The news is a surprise move by the tech giant, which had previously remarked that Huang, the company’s longtime CEO, wouldn’t be coming back after his resignation earlier this month.

As stated in Nvidia’s official press release, the board made its decision following a series of discussions with Huang.

Additionally, the organization consulted with high-ranking U.S. government officials to determine that the reappointment would not present a national security concern.

Huang himself acknowledged the reappointment, thanking employees, shareholders and the company’s leaders.

“I can’t wait to get back to work,” stated Huang.

The company also said that the independent inquiry into the events leading to Huang’s departure would continue.

The news of Huang’s reappointment comes as Nvidia shares were already recovering from their recent decline. Nvidia stock was up some 8% in premarket trading.

The news comes as crypto markets start to bounce back after several days of intense selling pressure.

As per the supplied market snapshot, Bitcoin is trading at $62,795.99, up 1.5% in the last hour.

Still, the biggest cryptocurrency is up just 0.3% in the last 24 hours and down 5% over the past week.

Recent findings suggest that on the brighter side, XRP is up 2% in the last hour at $0.9691. The Ripple-associated coin is 1.2% higher over the past 24 hours, though it is still down 1.8% over the past week.

According to recent reports, shiba Inu is also trading at $0.00000362. The coin has recorded a small daily increase of around 0.8%, as per CoinGlass data.

Other major crypto assets are also bouncing back. Ethereum is up 1.8% in the last hour at $1,767. Solana, meanwhile, is up 2.2% at $74.69.

The move higher comes after Bitcoin dropped to around $55,500 this past weekend, falling to its lowest price in over two years.

Another XRP Record Ahead? Ripple CEO Predicts XRP Demand Surge as Inflation-Stricken Markets Seek Alternatives to Fiat

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (582 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zycrypto

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that XRP could be on the verge of another major adoption milestone as inflation-hit economies increasingly look for alternatives to traditional currencies.
  • The Ripple frontman sees growing potential for the cryptocurrency, arguing that demand could rise over time as people in struggling markets seek ways to protect their wealth from weakening fiat currencies.
  • Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse believes inflation-hit economies could become an increasingly important source of demand for XRP as people seek alternatives to traditional currencies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that XRP could be on the verge of another major adoption milestone as inflation-hit economies increasingly look for alternatives to traditional currencies. At least that’s according to Brad Garlinghouse.

The Ripple frontman sees growing potential for the cryptocurrency, arguing that demand could rise over time as people in struggling markets seek ways to protect their wealth from weakening fiat currencies. His comments spotlight a potential upcoming driver of XRP adoption and raise fresh questions about how far demand could grow.

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse believes inflation-hit economies could become an increasingly important source of demand for XRP as people seek alternatives to traditional currencies. Speaking during a recent interview with Bloomberg Television at the Singapore FinTech Festival, he explained how persistent inflation and declining purchasing power could encourage more people to explore digital assets.

“XRP is going to draw people’s interest over time, particularly in markets where you have more inflationary dynamics,” he opined.

Garlinghouse argued that the declining value of fiat currencies could make assets with predictable or limited supplies more attractive to investors. To illustrate his point, he cited the U.S. dollar, describing it as one of the world’s best-managed currencies while noting that it had lost approximately half its value over the past decade.

It has been revealed that he added that the situation is considerably worse in countries with weaker monetary management, where some national currencies have reportedly lost between 80% and 90% of their value. Such conditions, in his view, could strengthen the appeal of digital assets whose supplies cannot be expanded at the discretion of central banks or governments.

However, scarcity alone is not enough to attract investors. Garlinghouse also highlighted liquidity as an notable consideration, noting that people want assets they can easily hold, transfer, and exchange. This combination could work in XRP’s favor as interest in alternative financial assets grows across inflation-hit markets.

In a recent development, his remarks point to a potential source of XRP demand beyond speculative trading and institutional investment. While increased interest does not guarantee sustained buying pressure or higher prices, broader adoption in economies struggling with currency depreciation could ultimately boost XRP’s long-term appeal.

During the interview, Amin also asked Garlinghouse whether he could see Bitcoin eventually rocketing to the $1 million mark, a target previously floated by several prominent figures in the crypto industry.

The Ripple chief was receptive to the possibility, although he admitted that predicting when such a milestone might happen was difficult. His optimism was largely rooted in the declining purchasing power of traditional currencies rather than any specific Bitcoin price model.

In a recent development, bitcoin has a hard supply cap of 21 million coins, while XRP’s total supply was established at 100 billion tokens. Their fixed supply structures distinguish them from government-issued currencies, which can be expanded through monetary policy.

Nevertheless, scarcity does not automatically translate into higher valuations or make either cryptocurrency immune to inflation. Both Bitcoin and XRP remain highly volatile assets whose prices are influenced by market demand and broader economic conditions.

It has been revealed that bitcoin surged above $64,400 as it extended its weekend recovery following Friday’s sharp drop below $56,000, while Ripple’s XRP also staged a rebound, briefly reaching $1.02, per CoinGecko. However, both cryptocurrencies have since surrendered part of those gains. At the time of writing, BTC had pulled back to around $61,271, while XRP had also retreated to $0.9435, reflecting renewed selling pressure after the brief recovery.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Home » Trendsetter News » XRP ETF Shares Surface in Schwab’s Repo Collateral.
  • XRP ETF shares just appeared in collateral baskets pledged by JPMorgan & Bank of America to a Schwab money market fund.
  • XRP exchange-traded fund shares appeared in collateral baskets posted by JPMorgan and Bank of America to a Schwab money market fund, according to wealth coach Kamilah Stevenson.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Trendsetter News » XRP ETF Shares Surface in Schwab’s Repo Collateral.

XRP ETF shares just appeared in collateral baskets pledged by JPMorgan & Bank of America to a Schwab money market fund.

XRP exchange-traded fund shares appeared in collateral baskets posted by JPMorgan and Bank of America to a Schwab money market fund, according to wealth coach Kamilah Stevenson.

In her latest YouTube episode, she argues that the reported holdings point to a less visible source of institutional demand: securities pledged against loans rather than bought for price exposure.

In a recent development, the distinction matters. Stevenson claims Schwab did not buy XRP or the ETFs outright; its fund lent cash and received baskets of securities backing the transactions.

Citing monthly SEC disclosures, Stevenson identifies XRP ETF shares from Grayscale, Canary, Franklin and Bitwise among collateral supplied by the banks’ trading arms.

She puts their combined value at roughly $36,000 in April, $2 million in June and more than $8 million by August, an increase exceeding 200-fold.

Those figures remain claims presented in the video. The transcript does not specify the reporting year or filing identifiers, limiting verification of the sequence.

Stevenson acknowledges that the positions were small relative to the underlying loans. Their inclusion would demonstrate acceptance of particular ETF securities within collateral baskets, not necessarily an institutional commitment to holding XRP directly.

The YouTube video episode connects those reported positions to BlackRock’s effort to expand acceptance of tokenized fund shares as collateral. Dr. Stevenson says the appeal is straightforward: investors could pledge income-producing fund shares instead of redeeming them to provide cash.

Sources indicate that she also points to Binance’s acceptance of BlackRock’s BUIDL fund as collateral and describes a wider shift toward blockchain-based collateral transfers. Her thesis is that assets used to secure financing can generate more persistent demand than assets held solely for trading.

It has been revealed that “Trading creates excitement; collateral creates demand that stays,” Dr. Stevenson states.

That argument needs a boundary. Acceptance of XRP ETF shares does not establish that lenders accept XRP itself, and tokenized collateral does not automatically require XRP to move between markets. Stevenson presents direct XRP-backed lending and cross-currency settlement as potential next steps, not completed developments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shiba Inu (SHIB) gained 5.96% over the past 24 hours and traded at $0.0000038 on Monday, according to CoinMarketCap, as talk of a December "Santa rally" returned to the crypto market. Still, SHIB is down 8.86% over the past seven days, and the token has lost 18.5% in November so far, according to CryptoRank.

Last week, SHIB dropped to $0.00000337, its lowest level since 2021.

Sources indicate that the hopes for a Santa rally come after Goldman Sachs analysts noted last week that most of the December gains on the stock market usually come after Dec. 15. SHIB's own December history, however, shows that the Santa rally came for the token once in five years.

According to CryptoRank, SHIB lost 29.5% and 13.5% in December of 2021 and 2022, respectively. In December of 2023, the token gained 24.6%. In December of 2024 and 2025, SHIB lost 21% and 17.6%, respectively.

SHIB's median December return is -17.6%, and its average December return is -11.4%, according to CryptoRank data.

Sources indicate that the green December of 2023 came after SHIB gained 6.04% in October and 6.62% in November of that year, according to CryptoRank. In 2026, SHIB lost 18.6% in October, and November is also in the red so far.

Industry observers note that the Goldman note, titled "GS Flow of Funds: Chopsgiving," came from Gail Hafif, Brian Garrett and Lee Coppersmith, who looked at S&P 500 data going back to 1928. According to the note, the index usually gains 1.1% from mid-November to early December and then gives back about two-thirds of that gain by mid-December, and around 80% of the full 2.4% gain comes after Dec. 14-15.

Since 1990, the S&P 500 has risen after Dec. 15 in 27 of 36 years, according to Goldman.

The Goldman team called these figures a historical map. In the years when the VIX volatility index was above 18 in the middle of November, the S&P 500 gained 1.34% on average, and the index ended the year higher in 59% of cases, according to the note. According to Goldman, the VIX was above that level in mid-November of this year as well.

Recent findings suggest that goldman also said that retail investors have been buying major tech and chip stocks. Large funds and systematic traders have been cutting their positions, according to the note.

Sources indicate that the Stock Trader's Almanac counts the last five trading days of December and the first two trading days of January as the Santa Claus rally. This season, the window will open on Dec. 24 and close on Jan. 5.

Recent findings suggest that in the window that ended on Jan. 5, 2026, the S&P 500 declined 0.11%, according to the Almanac. "Santa was a no-show for the third year in a row," the Almanac wrote. Before that, the S&P 500 also ended the Santa Claus rally windows of 2023 and 2024 lower.

Bitcoin might not be out of the woods yet, despite recently staging a relief rally toward $60,000 after renewed market optimism over Nvidia’s announcement that it is reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO and president.

Market analyst Crypto with Sarmad believes Bitcoin’s next four-year cycle bottom could form around $41,000.

According to the analyst, if BTC continues following its historical cycle pattern, another notable decline could be ahead before the market establishes a formidable bottom.

Adding to the concerns, on-chain analytics provider Tranquility Crypto has identified a bearish cup-and-handle formation on Bitcoin’s weekly chart.

The pattern’s neckline sits around $60,000, making it a critical level for determining BTC’s next direction, since a confirmed breakdown could expose Bitcoin to a deeper correction toward $36,000.

Meanwhile, analyst SeffafNet recently outlined another potential downside target of $49,000, identifying several support levels that could come into play if selling pressure accelerates.

The analyst also anticipated the possibility of one final capitulation event before bulls return in full gear and potentially trigger a broader recovery.

According to CoinCodex data, BTC is trading at $60,404, placing it close to the critical $60,000 neckline identified by Tranquility Crypto.

Why is Bitcoin’s short-term price action key? Holding above $60,000 could help Bitcoin avoid an immediate bearish breakdown, while losing this psychological level could deepen its woes and set up another leg lower.

Recent findings suggest that the best outdoor gifts also function as great gifts for dads, smart gifts for men, and (of course) perfect gifts for camping. Whether he’s a nature novice or a seasoned mountain man chopping his own wood, we've collected all our field notes from rigorous testing in the past year to assemble the best gifts for outdoorsmen at every level and price point. Keep scrolling to get to the good stuff and don't put it off, as we're getting down to the wire for holiday gifting.

These electric hand warmers hold about 16 hours of steady warmth. What's cool is they stick together via a magnet for easy storage so you'll never lose one and be without it.

The Lifestraw Peak Series will eliminate approximately 99.999 percent of bacteria, parasites, microplastics, sand, and dirt. Gift this personal water filter as a stocking stuffer, or buy multiple and pass them out to all of the outdoorsmen in your life.

In a recent development, nike blew us away with the release of this trail running shoe. Don’t be fooled by the low profile, because while sleek, this shoe is grippy, grounded, and up for just about any terrain you throw at it. We liked the extra toe room as well as how the sole functions more like shock absorbers than the base of a shoe, taking bump after bump while keeping your feet plenty comfortable. Whether you’re barreling down a hill or zigzagging up a steep slope, these shoes will give you an added boost and keep you both cool and stable.

It has been revealed that now, this is a cool adventure gift. The Nanopresso Portable Espresso Maker brings you top-quality coffee wherever you go. Just bring your favorite coffee grounds, add hot water, and this little machine does the rest. As you pump, the pressure is made, and thus, so is your drink. And at smaller than the size of a thermos, you can fit this just about anywhere.

Ah, the rancher jacket. It’s a double-sided gem, one that both looks the part but delivers even in the most rugged conditions. This fine option from Flint and Tinder is flannel-lined to fend off the chilly bite, as well as quilted and stuffed with insulation for good measure. That means even the nastiest of winds won’t bother him while he’s out chopping wood for the campfire. The roomy build means he can layer appropriately underneath and the fact that it demonstrates a little age with a nice patina over time is a big plus. He’ll be way ready for winter with his jacket.

Take all the bear-, weather-, and bomb-proofness of Yeti’s Loadout GoBox (and coolers) and shrink it down to a 1-liter case that’s perfect for phones, wallets, watches, AirPods, protein bars, or anything for your EDC. Strappable through an integrated tether strap, it can attach and lock to just about anything you can think of. I've used it so far on camping trips to go screen-free, as well as a few canoe rides where I still wanted to have my phone around (but avoid it getting wet).

Sources indicate that A big part of nailing the marks in the outdoor apparel realm is conquering both flexibility and insulation. You know, like this stretchy number from Mountain Hardwear. It’s plenty warm, packs down like a charm, and moves with your natural motions, never pulling or tugging. It helps that it looks sharp and touts elastic cuff bindings to lock in the warmth on those chilly evenings and mornings. This one is a great gift for all types of outdoorsmen, from campers and hikers to anglers and skiers. We found that the climbers here at MH especially liked this one, drawn to the agile design.

This will come in handy for spontaneous adventurers. It’s a handy, pocket-sized kit that has 48 tools useful in almost any outdoor survival situation. Plus, it looks like a freakin' grenade. How gift-worthy is that?

Camp Snap brings a bit of that retro joy to your outdoor adventures. A screen-free device, it makes you wait (in gleeful anticipation) to see the results of your photographic eye. It also comes in cool, earthy color tones and packs well with all of his other adventuring gear. The latest model is 15% thinner, making it even more portable and can knock out 500 images in a single charge. There’s even a kid-friendly setting and don’t worry, you can still access six different filters to get that perfect filter you’re after. With that screen-free business, he really will enjoy his surroundings more and focus less on that instant gratification (while still documenting treks with great pictures).

No, you’re not saying he’s old with this gift. Rather, you’re rewarding his intrepid spirit and encouraging him to venture even deeper into those topsy-turvy trails. The best way to do so is with a proper pair of trekking poles, which essentially afford an extra set of legs as you navigate harsh terrain. With three sections per pole linked by an internal cord, the design is smart as they fold and the tungsten carbide tips dig into the trail like a pair of eagle talons. Portable, lightweight, and strong, you can pull these puppies out of your pack and deploy them in an instant with a single button press.

It has been revealed that the best of the outdoors is usually an off-the-grid sort of thing but a little tech can help you enjoy remote areas even more. Take the latest from Garmin, part of an esteemed line of communication devices that can go deep, deep into the brush. If that outdoorsy someone on your list likes the backcountry, this is a vital addition to his setup. Fit with a digital touchscreen and able to send messages (text and voice) and SOS notes without any service, it’s all about location and safety. The Mini 3 can even send images, use voice commands in various languages, pair up with your smartphone, and send emergency notes 24/7. Oh, and it’s tough as nails, has a strong battery, and can even set you up with the weather forecast.

Here’s a pair for the trail-running novice and seasoned vet alike. The shoe combines comfort, support, durability, and a decidedly stylish look that has no trouble gobbling up mile after mile on the dusty (or muddy, or rocky) trail. On the surface, you get some serious colorways and a toothy but not over-the-top look. Under the hood, an improved midsole that rebounds like an NBA-level power forward and dual mid-foot webbing reinforcements to assist those active feet. And the details add up, from the padded collar to the stay-in-place tongue wings, making for a smooth trek even way, way down (or up) the trail.

What takes a hoodie into the high-performance echelon and helps it excel there? Extremely breathable and temperature-regulating fleece, genuine ripstop shell fabric, and a pair of warming pockets. Oh, and the raglan sleeves and elastic ends keep things comfortable and secure the warmth. It’s an added bonus that the fit is just about perfect, the hood wears brilliantly, and the whole thing can fend off even the thickest brush and snags. As Marmot rightfully claims, this one breathes like a feather and feels like a fleece. Usually it’s one or the other but not here. Gift this one to that restless outdoorsy soul who stays active year-round.

It has been revealed that taking the enhanced vision category into the unexpected realm of cool, Nocs is up to good work. The latest binocular set fits the bill, with powerful lenses and a textured design that’s easy to carry (and even easier on the eyes). Waterproof, they can accompany any trek, on land or water, in summer or winter, and that goes for all types of outdoors enthusiasts, from casual birders and hikers to backcountry pros and road trippers who like to hit the pullouts and take it all in. Compact with full-size clarity, these binocs do what many twice their size try to do, so store ’em in a small pack or wear ‘em over your neck with ease.

It has been revealed that flannels are a staple in an outdoorsman's wardrobe. If he has yet to try Outerknown's Blanket Shirt, now is the time to gift him one. They come in a ton of colors and are woven in a way that has just the right warmth and softness, without ever going too extreme. Call it the Goldilocks flannel.

Recent findings suggest that you really can’t miss with a trusty multitool. And there’s no more trusty versions out there than the Skeletool CX from Leatherman. It’s lightweight at just five ounces and sports seven different tools: a steel blade, pliers, wire cutters, a customizable bit driver, and a dual carabiner/bottle opener. That’ll serve anyone’s everyday needs pretty well.

Sources indicate that we love this fresh book from Max Humphrey, a real celebration of all things Yellowstone. Unlike many coffee table books, this one makes you feel like you’re actually sharing a car with the author and touring the Park, taking in great panoramas of lodges, bison jams, mountain vistas, and more. Perhaps that’s the attention to details and fresh perspective you get from an interior designer like Humphrey. If you like this one, consider his other book on the Great Smoky Mountains.

Recent findings suggest that if they're a runner, they're going to need a few things to continue that before-or-after-work pursuit during the winter months. A headlamp is one of those items, as dark runs need light. The latest offering from BioLite is super light at 2.6 ounces, has a comfortable strap, and holds a ton of charge at 200 hours of runtime. And the best part? I haven't had it shaking or bouncing on me once yet.

Stellar recorded $207.2 million in tokenized funds in the seven days to November 22, reaffirming continued institutional interest in the blockchain.

Sources indicate that the RWA Foundation shared data in a post using figures from Token Terminal showing that Stellar ranked among the top blockchains in tokenized fund growth in the seven days from November 15 to November 22, 2026. Stellar recorded $207.2 million: Franklin Templeton added $108.0 million and Spiko added $68.2 million.

Industry observers note that .@injective led tokenized fund growth this past week. @StellarOrg had a good week also. https://t.co/7Ip2oK6c1X.

This means Stellar continues to grow in tokenized assets, a major highlight of strong growth in Q3, 2026.

Real-world assets tokenized on Stellar amounted to $4.1 billion at the end of Q3 2026, up 36% from Q2 and up 548% from Q3 2025. Two assets drove the bulk of the quarter’s growth: Tradable’s new tokenized private credit and continued inflows into the Spiko Amundi overnight swap fund.

In late August 2026, Stellar held more tokenized non-US government debt than any other blockchain, with about $490 million in sovereign instruments. These included Spiko’s euro Treasury bill fund, Mexican CETES and Brazilian Tesouro bonds through Etherfuse, South Korean Treasury bonds, and a Marshall Islands digital sovereign bond.

Industry observers note that stellar has widened access to tokenized funds in the United States, Europe and Asia. Franklin Templeton’s BENJI has been on Stellar since 2021. In August 2026, the SEC's Division of Investment Management issued a no-action letter confirming that the Franklin Templeton's registered mutual funds and ETFs may use BENJI for cash management. This expands the set of institutions permitted to hold it. Franklin Templeton made a similar move in Europe, registering 'grBenji' as a Luxembourg UCITS share class for third-party distribution, now live on 21X.

According to recent reports, in Asia, Marketnode unveiled in August that it will offer funds from BNY Investments on Stellar, with Marketnode acting as the tokenization and distribution platform. Together, these developments expand access to tokenized funds on Stellar for institutions in the United States, Europe and Asia.

State Street Investment Management and Galaxy brought their Onchain Liquidity Sweep Fund to Stellar in September 2026.

The past weeks have seen the broad crypto ETF market face consistent withdrawals from investors, causing Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Solana, and others to record steady outflows since October.

While the negative trend has continued, Solana has just taken over the leadership in the broad ETF market after recording its first inflow in a while.

Latest data from SosoValue demonstrates that while Bitcoin, Ethereum, and XRP ETFs have continued to struggle with consistent weekly outflows, Solana has just beaten the trend after it finally ended a six-week streak of consecutive weekly outflows.

Notably, the data reveals that Solana spot ETFs have recorded a net inflow of $4.38 million over the week.

Although the net amount of capital received by the ETFs appears decent, it is significant considering the growing crypto market weakness.

While this marks an end to the Solana ETFs' six-week outflow streak, this is the first positive weekly performance they have recorded since October 9.

Further data shows that Bitcoin spot ETFs suffered the largest withdrawals as investors pulled out about $1.79 billion during the same period.

The negative trend also extended to the Ethereum ETF market as the funds posted a total of $314.17 million in net outflows following the consistent selling pressure.

In addition to this, the XRP spot ETFs were not spared, as the funds recorded $11.11 million in weekly outflows, leaving Solana as the only one among the four major crypto ETFs to finish the week on a positive note.

Veteran trader Peter Brandt has softened the tone of his recent Bitcoin warnings and remarked on X that the cryptocurrency held at the level it needed to hold after its drop to $55,150 over the weekend.

"Bitcoin held exactly where it had to hold -- for now anyway, but perhaps for more than now," Brandt wrote on Monday.

Brandt also shared a monthly chart of Bitcoin together with the post. The chart goes back to 2018, and Brandt marked on it the same patterns that he had already pointed to in previous years. According to the chart, the price of Bitcoin was back above $63,000 at the time of the post and stood at $63,338.

On Saturday, Bitcoin fell as low as $55,150. It was the lowest price of the cryptocurrency since September 2024, and before that, the lowest price of Bitcoin in 2026 was $57,718 on July 1, according to Coinbase.

According to recent reports, on Nov. 15, Brandt posted a weekly chart with a possible head-and-shoulders top and stated that, if the pattern proves valid, Bitcoin's October 2025 record of about $126,000 may not be surpassed in his lifetime. Two days before that, on Nov. 13, Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 for the first time since August.

Sources indicate that brandt has also pointed to the history of Bitcoin's bull market cycles more than once. Late last year, he posted a chart showing that each of Bitcoin's five major bull runs began after drawdowns of 75% or more, and he wrote that if the decline carried to $50,000, "the next bull market cycle should carry to $200k to $250K.".

In April, Brandt remarked that Bitcoin could form an "investable low" in September or October 2026. According to Brandt, this low may or may not go below the February low near $60,000, and the next cycle peak could land between $300,000 and $500,000 in September or October 2029 if the four-year cycle continues to hold.

"Real bottom will not occur until October 2026," Brandt stated in an interview in February.

It has been revealed that the latest Brandt post comes amid a rally in U.S. tech stocks on Monday. Earlier that day, Nvidia announced that its board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, chief executive officer and board member, effective immediately.

According to the Nvidia announcement, the board received input from senior levels of the U.S. government before the decision, and it is confident that Huang's return "poses no national security risk." Shares of Nvidia surged 33% after the news, according to CNBC.

Bitcoin went up together with tech stocks and briefly climbed above $64,000 on Monday. Before the Nvidia news, Bitcoin had already recovered from the Saturday low to around $61,500.

Huang resigned from Nvidia on Nov. 12. On Nov. 17, Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones noted on the firm's earnings call that the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that last week, Bitcoin [BTC] fell to a low of $55,130 on Saturday, the 20th of November. This was lower than $57,800, which the leading crypto registered on the 1st of July.

It led to debate around whether the bear market was truly over, or whether what we saw in August-September was only a pause within the longer-term bearish trend.

Over the past two weeks, Bitcoin liquidations exceeded $600 million on four separate days.

Sources indicate that the 11th and the 20th of November, when BTC breached key support levels at $73k and $61.4k, saw the heaviest long liquidations. Also, contextually speaking, these two days witnessed $690 million and $670 million in long liquidations, respectively.

The persistent downward price action was accompanied by relentless selling. Since the 5th of November, every trading day bar one has seen negative spot ETF flows.

It has been revealed that last week’s net outflows alone reached $1.245 billion. This incessant selling would need to ease before Bitcoin could find room to recover.

In a recent development, as things stand, a weekly trading session close below $57,800 is needed to flip the structure bearishly. The previous week’s correction, though deep, might be just a liquidity sweep before a recovery.

Bitcoin holders are under severe strain as prices approach or drop below their cost basis, and Open Interest has plunged dramatically. It was a result of tightening monetary policy and the global equity market downturn.

Over the past year, the BTC Open Interest was down by $4.5 billion.

Industry observers note that in July, this figure fell as low as $6.5 billion. It was the largest OI downturn in Bitcoin’s history in dollar terms, observed crypto analyst Darkfost.

Sources indicate that there have been eight trading days in 2026 with over $1.5 billion in liquidations across the crypto market. A decline in risk appetite among investors, several liquidation cascades, and the overarching bearish price action for most of the year helped explain the OI drop.

A leverage reset can be healthy for the market.

In a recent development, alongside the weekly BTC chart, there was hope for a bear market bottom. Even so, it remains risky to buy, as a bear market continuation cannot yet be fully ruled out.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite the sharp fall in the cryptocurrency market, Michael Saylor-led Strategy has not stopped its Bitcoin (BTC) buying spree, as it picked up 457 BTC worth around $29.6 million.

The firm's recent purchase comes as the leading cryptocurrency has been struggling to rebound from the heavy sell-off that recently dragged it to a two-plus-year low.

The latest data from Strategy's SEC filing reveals that the firm has bought 457 Bitcoin at an average price of $64,898 per coin.

The newly introduced purchase brings Strategy’s Bitcoin holdings to around 851,305 BTC, which accounts for over 4% of the cryptocurrency's maximum supply of 21 million coins.

The firm has now spent around $64.23 billion to build its Bitcoin holdings at an average price of $75,446 per Bitcoin.

It is worth noting that Strategy has been buying BTC at gradually decreasing prices as the cryptocurrency market continues to bleed heavily.

On Nov. 2, the firm confirmed that it had bought 811 BTC, worth around $65.5 million, at an average price of $80,846 per Bitcoin.

Recent findings suggest that A week later, on Nov. 9, Strategy unveiled the purchase of 1,036 BTC worth $81.9 million at an average price of $79,012.

The firm’s Bitcoin purchase a week later, on Nov. 16, was relatively smaller at 485 BTC, worth $33.4 million, with an average price of $68,887.

Recent findings suggest that the newly introduced 457 BTC purchase continues this pattern. The latest Strategy purchase was made at an almost 20% lower price than the firm’s Nov. 2 acquisition.

Overall, the firm has made four weekly purchases, scooping up around 2,789 BTC worth $210.4 million.

In a recent development, however, these purchases have been much smaller than before. The latest $29.6 million purchase is almost 64% lower than the $81.9 million purchase announced just two weeks ago.

Although Saylor is doubling down on Bitcoin, Strategy’s massive holdings in the cryptocurrency are underwater as the market has been struggling to regain its footing.

In a recent development, on Nov. 21, Bitcoin hit a low of around $55,130, its lowest level since September 2024, before rebounding above $61,000.

The firm’s recent purchases have helped reduce its overall average Bitcoin acquisition cost, but the drop has not been that significant.

For example, with the latest purchase, the average cost of the firm’s Bitcoin holdings dropped from $75,452 to around $75,446, a decline of just $6 per Bitcoin.

At the same time, the firm has also been putting a lot of resources into supporting its preferred securities.

In the latest reporting period, Strategy sold around 1.93 million common shares, raising net proceeds of $176.7 million.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that is THIS dip a good time to invest? One analyst thinks so.

Bitcoin’s Fear & Greed Index stood at 11, compared to 50 in early November, reflecting a sharp shift in market sentiment alongside BTC’s 20% correction. Long-term investors may benefit from this as many weak holders are offloading their BTC. This allows large investors to take up the BTC on sale, allowing them to buy it cheaper.

Against this backdrop, Michael Saylor’s recent post showing his famous Bitcoin buying signal suggests whales may be getting into the market.

With BTC falling toward $56k, extreme fear, and Strategy’s continued purchases, it does lend some support to the analyst’s view that this dip could be a buying opportunity.

But the bigger question remains: Does buying the dip offer enough long-term upside?

In terms of on-chain and technical indicators, BTC has seen a 40% pullback from its post-election rally in 2024. From a long-term perspective, it has also pulled back to levels seen 5 years prior.

This means Bitcoin has erased years of price gains, raising questions about whether the recent correction can be viewed as a buying opportunity or if it is indicative of a deeper market downturn.

Industry observers note that simply put, does Bitcoin’s long-term return profile justify Michael Saylor’s latest purchase and analysts’ bullish outlook? Or could weakening returns and a prolonged price decline discourage smart money from accumulating Bitcoin [BTC]?

Key onchain signals are already showing a divergence from the analysts’ bullish outlook.

While there is extreme fear in the market, a whale moved 2,279 BTC into Binance, while another whale took a 40x BTC short worth $91 million.

In a recent development, extreme fear has historically attracted bargain hunters. However, these whale transactions suggested some large investors were preparing for further downside.

In a recent development, meanwhile, Bitcoin’s supply distribution painted an equally concerning picture. Nearly 57% of BTC’s supply was sitting at a loss, leaving just 43% in profit.

However, large players are taking a more risk-averse stance, making the possibility of further capitulation harder to ignore.

Ultimately, extreme fear alone may not be enough to confirm a bottom. This puts Saylor’s latest Bitcoin buy signal in a different light.

With BTC’s long-term structure weakening, limited signs of whale accumulation, and capitulation risks rising, buying the dip may carry more downside risk than potential upside.

Extreme fear and Strategy’s continued Bitcoin purchases suggest a potential buying opportunity, but they do not confirm a market bottom.

Rising supply in loss, whale selling, and large short positions point to further downside and capitulation risks.

Recent findings suggest that on Monday, XRP briefly rose above $1 after the return of Jensen Huang to Nvidia sparked a rally on Wall Street and a wave of short liquidations in the crypto market. At the peak of the move, short liquidations on XRP exceeded long liquidations by 578%, according to CoinGlass data.

On the XRPUSDT perpetual contract on Binance, the price of XRP went from $0.94 to as high as $1.02 within minutes after 14:00 UTC, and later it pulled back and stood at $0.984, according to TradingView.

According to recent reports, earlier on Monday, before the opening bell, Nvidia confirmed that its board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately. The firm said that the board was satisfied with Huang's "candor and ability to lead" after a series of meetings with him, and that its independent investigation would continue. According to the company, the board received input from senior U.S. government officials and concluded that Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk.".

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones noted in a statement.

Huang resigned as CEO on Nov. 12, and on Nov. 17, during the tech giant's earnings call, Jones said that the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

In premarket trading, Nvidia stock jumped 27% to $159.48 as of 9 a.m. ET, and at the start of U.S. trading on Monday, Nvidia shares were up more than 30%. The rally spread across Wall Street, and the S&P 500 rose as much as 5.6% and the Nasdaq 100 as much as 7.9%, according to NBC News.

Industry observers note that coinGlass data indicates that $9.45 million worth of XRP positions were liquidated over the past 24 hours, and $7.18 million of that amount came from short positions. Long positions accounted for $2.27 million.

In a recent development, the same happened across the rest of the crypto market. In total, 110,663 traders were liquidated for $660.89 million over the past 24 hours, according to CoinGlass, and shorts accounted for $515.94 million of that amount.

Bitcoin led the list with $273.26 million in liquidations, and 82.8% of that amount came from short positions. Ethereum followed with $139.07 million, and Solana was third with $24.93 million.

Besides, perpetual contracts on Nvidia stock and on SOXL, a triple-leveraged exchange-traded fund on semiconductor stocks, were next on the list with $16.34 million and $15.01 million in liquidations, respectively, according to CoinGlass.

Industry observers note that while the wider market recovery may have helped NIGHT, the token’s 13.25% gain suggests a more isolated type of buying interest. Whether the token is able to maintain this surge and potentially break $0.053 really depends on buyers’ continued demand and how well Bitcoin holds its recent recovery.

It has been revealed that the token has largely traded within a $0.035-$0.053 range since October, suggesting an established consolidation in which buyers have repeatedly defended lower prices. This range has also limited upward advances, with the $0.053 area acting as a ceiling for the past two months.

Industry observers note that the latest recovery has brought NIGHT towards its upper boundary once again. If the move above this range is sustained, it could signal a shift in market structure and open the door to further gains.

The RSI has recovered to 62.09, hinting at strengthening bullish momentum, and the OBV’s recent uptrend suggests that buying volume is supporting the token’s recovery.

In a recent development, looking at the H4 chart, NIGHT fell to $0.03896 on November 21 but made a quick recovery over the following two days. It has since reclaimed the 78.6% Fibonacci retracement at $0.04863, recovering most of its previous decline, bringing its previous swing high back into focus.

Industry observers note that the shift in momentum is also reflecting on the MACD as its moved above both its signal and zero lines. Furthermore, the OBV continued its upward trend, suggesting that buyers are slowly starting to re-enter the market, helping sustain the move higher.

It has been revealed that NIGHT is now approaching its previous H4 swing high at $0.05126. Breaking above this level gives the bulls another shot at pushing out of the token’s two-month consolidation as it puts the daily range resistance at $0.05315 within reach.

However, another rejection would send NIGHT lower, with the daily 50% Fibonacci level at $0.03795 becoming the next support.

  • 23 announcement, the DOJ said that it has filed a civil forfeiture complaint to recover over $1.1 billion worth of stolen cryptocurrency as part of its efforts to retrieve the billions lost in the massive hack.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The United States Department of Justice (DOJ) has initiated a significant legal push to address the theft of over $6 billion worth of cryptocurrency from Binance by North Korean hackers last month.

As per a Nov. 23 announcement, the DOJ said that it has filed a civil forfeiture complaint to recover over $1.1 billion worth of stolen cryptocurrency as part of its efforts to retrieve the billions lost in the massive hack.

The recent development comes less than a month after North Korean hackers reportedly broke into Binance on Oct. 29 in one of the biggest crypto heists ever.

The DOJ claimed that its recent civil forfeiture action focuses on over $1.1 billion worth of USD Coin (USDC), a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar and issued by Circle.

The assets are alleged to have been stolen from Binance and laundered by North Korean cybercriminals.

Industry observers note that significantly, the assets had previously been frozen under a restraining order obtained by the government earlier this month. With the fresh court filing, the potential recovery of the assets has taken another step forward.

Sources indicate that the DOJ further claimed that U.S. authorities have successfully helped freeze, seize or return over $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency since the attack in October.

This is nearly half of the total $6 billion-plus stolen from Binance, though the government did not provide details about how much of that has been returned to the exchange.

According to recent reports, the importance of collaboration between law enforcement agencies and crypto firms to ensure that hackers don't get away with stolen assets was stressed by Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva.

According to recent reports, “North Korean cyber hackers stole over $6 billion of cryptocurrency from Binance. But prompt coordination with both the government and our private sector partners helped to avoid the bulk of these assets from being lost,” Duva noted.

U.S. authorities have further revealed the sophisticated money laundering techniques used by North Korean hackers to conceal their stolen cryptocurrency.

FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman noted that the regime uses intricate money laundering methods to convert stolen digital assets into funds for its illicit activities.

After the Binance hack, authorities rapidly worked to trace the stolen funds and coordinate with crypto service providers to block further transfers.

The U.S. Secret Service claimed that its investigators were able to detect and freeze some of the stolen funds within minutes of the hack.

Sources indicate that "The bad actors in this intrusion thought they could run from law enforcement. They've found out they were wrong," remarked Secret Service Special Agent in Charge Todd Bratz.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Crypto Market News » Why Bitcoin Fell Below $60K Despite Nvidia’s 31% Surge.

While tech stocks celebrated Jensen Huang’s return, on-chain metrics suggest crypto traders face a very different test.

Bitcoin (BTC) briefly fell to $59,400 after failing to sustain a rally triggered by Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO —largely because the bounce was fueled by short-lived enthusiasm rather than genuine spot demand or improved crypto fundamentals.

While Nvidia (NVDA) shares surged more than 30% and major U.S. stock indexes recorded one of their best sessions in years on Monday, November 23, Bitcoin’s price reversed its initial recovery within about 12 hours, raising questions about buying demand across the cryptocurrency market.

In a recent development, bitcoin climbed toward an intraday high of $64,500 following Nvidia’s announcement before retreating below $60,000. The reversal contrasted with Nvidia’s 31% gain, the Nasdaq’s 6.51% advance and the S&P 500’s 4.73% increase.

According to Santiment’s latest market intelligence report, Bitcoin’s initial recovery was driven mainly by a wave of optimism and FOMO across financial markets, rather than any real improvement in demand for BTC.

Santiment’s Trending Words Dashboard recorded a sharp increase in mentions of Nvidia and Jensen Huang across cryptocurrency discussions on November 23, producing the largest single-day spike over the past month.

Recent findings suggest that “Huang’s return provided an immediate reason for investors to become more confident in Nvidia and its surrounding AI ecosystem,” the Santiment report states. “However, nothing about the announcement directly improved Bitcoin’s adoption, increased demand for BTC, or resolved the selling pressure that had dominated cryptocurrency markets for weeks.”.

Still, the report noted that AI and big data altcoins could hold long-term potential. For Bitcoin, however, rather than confirming a new bullish trend, the rally became another example of how FOMO can punish traders who mistake a temporary market reaction for a lasting shift in fundamentals.

Despite the underwhelming price action, Santiment’s on-chain data highlighted an unexpected divergence.

Around November 20, the analytics firm recorded roughly 750,400 daily active addresses and 332,820 new addresses, pointing to a notable rise in network participation even as prices weakened.

Daily active addresses measure how many unique blockchain addresses participate in transactions, while network growth tracks newly created active addresses.

Both metrics climbed during the downturn, indicating that underlying blockchain usage remained resilient despite falling market value.

Sources indicate that santiment cautioned that the upcoming Thanksgiving holiday may introduce another layer of uncertainty. Trading activity typically thins out during holiday-shortened weeks, allowing smaller groups of buyers and sellers to trigger outsized price swings amid lower liquidity.

Markets are also looking ahead to Wednesday’s October PCE inflation report and the Federal Reserve’s Beige Book, both of which could shift rate expectations ahead of the Fed’s December 8–9 policy meeting.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin traders are watching for a potential retest of the $56,000 level, which could mark a local market bottom.

U.S. President Donald Trump wrapped up his third exclusive dinner for his biggest Official Trump [TRUMP] memecoin holders on the 22nd of November.

Hosted at Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia, the dinner offered access to the President and other prominent personalities to investors who held significant amounts of $TRUMP.

The top 185 holders qualified for the dinner, while the top 29 received invitations to a separate VIP reception. In fact, the top four were also promised an 18-karat gold Trump watch. This came after the November midterm elections, where Democrats swept the majority in both the House and Senate.

But this dinner is raising eyebrows like never before.

Sources indicate that this is because there was a sharp decline in participation. During the first $TRUMP memecoin gala in May 2025, eligible investors reportedly needed to hold at least $55,000 worth of tokens to qualify.

This time, one participant reportedly secured entry with just $518 worth of tokens.

Furthermore, more than 5,000 holders who could potentially have qualified did not even register, despite organizers extending the registration deadline by four days.

That said, the combined holdings of participants reportedly fell from $148 million in May 2025 to just $8.6 million for the latest gala.

Remarking on the same, Donald Sherman, president of Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington ( CREW), stated,.

Donald Trump’s memecoin dinner is the clearest evidence that he cares more about lining his pockets and giving access to his personal investors than addressing the problems facing the American public.

$TRUMP memecoin price action further reflected this momentum as it was trading below $1, compared with its peak of approximately $75. At press time, too, the memecoin was trading at $0.9005 after an 81.3% drop in the year so far.

That mentioned, the controversy goes beyond the declining price of a cryptocurrency. This is because the Democrats argue that Trump is using his position as president to financially benefit from businesses connected to his personal brand.

The concern is that investors may have purchased $TRUMP tokens not simply because of the memecoin itself, but because holding them could give them insider access.

Sources indicate that needless to say, eight Democratic senators, led by Adam Schiff, have already questioned Trump and his crypto ventures thanks to the insider activity and profit-making. As expected, they have also called for investigations into his crypto-related businesses.

All of this comes after the Trump family reportedly earned at least $635 million from the memecoin, according to previous reports from AMBCrypto.

Yet, despite these political differences, crypto continues to enjoy bipartisan support, with a good number of Democratic and Republican lawmakers backing digital assets.

With the deeper correction in the cryptocurrency market, we are finally witnessing somewhat of a bounce in multiple top-15 digital assets, including XRP, Monero and Dogecoin.

XRP is printing higher network usage compared to October, Monero is gradually outperforming the market in the last 24 hours and Dogecoin is aiming at a local price recovery, even though a modest one.

One crucial development that we haven't anticipated is Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia (NVDA) CEO on November 23, only 11 days after his resignation. The announcement triggered a substantial market retrace, with NVDA stock gaining over 30% and Nasdaq adding around 6.8%, recovering a large share of last week's losses.

Recent findings suggest that thankfully, XRP shows us resilience beyond regular market metrics: the average daily payments throughout the month have crossed the 1.1 million threshold, a 107% growth versus the October baseline. The basis behind the reversal is considerable: the rise in market volatility that triggered a substantial breakdown in the asset.

With rapid market swings, it's no surprise that the asset saw more than 1.33 million transactions throughout the first 7 days of the month. New accounts over a rolling 24-hour period reached 4,065 wallets, per XRPScan query on November 23.

In a recent development, from the technical standpoint, XRP is presently trading near the $0.99 price level, approximately 23% lower compared to the 30-day average, which fits the aforementioned bearish narrative. The decline in spot trading volume is also an crucial sign: spot investors dropped around 22.5% of their trading activities throughout the month.

The drop in futures volume also makes the picture slightly more complicated than it should be. Following the price breakdown, the volatility increase was followed by an increase in open interest, so the drop we're witnessing right now is more of a return to the baseline than an glitch on its own.

The current price resistance and support points are quite diverse, but not thoroughly tested, apart from a local support level at $0.9. The immediate breakout test is going to take place at approximately $0.99, with a possibility of a further recovery. The level at $1.00 is more of a psychological barrier, while $1.04 is the threshold that should mark the end of the downtrend.

According to CoinMarketCap's data, Monero has been steadily underperforming XRP and Dogecoin in the last 24 hours, though it's important to separate rising demand and active speculative buying. In the last 24 hours, Monero has gained over 4.7% in price. Futures open interest has crossed the $230 million mark.

Sources indicate that as already mentioned, Monero is a weaker performer out of the three, with a 4.7% gain over the last 24 hours. Unexpectedly, a deeper look reveals a set of challenges: spot and futures volume, open interest and liquidation volume suggest a rather stale market with no momentum rather than an explosive recovery that might turn into a proper uptrend. The good news is that most of the liquidated volume is on the short side.

In a recent development, from the network usage perspective, Monero is struggling, with its transaction count dropping below the 30-day average, prompting baseless price resilience. Though Monero's network design certainly limits the possibility of a thorough analysis due to its protected transaction design.

Industry observers note that the most key development around Monero was, of course, the most recent Wrapped Monero incident. Despite the wrapped token itself having little to do with the main network of the asset, the coin itself had to withstand the rippling selling pressure. The token lost more than 99% of its value, causing $13 million in losses.

The main network itself went through a security audit on November 18, which found no high- or medium-severity vulnerabilities and only minor security issues, which developers have been notified about.

If the technical side of the question is rather vital, the most important immediate price levels are the 508-510 range, which corresponds to the current breakout area, and the immediate support at $500.

According to recent reports, compared to all three cryptocurrencies, Monero is the only one showing some positivity over the last 7 days, despite the wrapped token incident. Privacy assets like XMR or Zcash quite often provide more market resilience during breakdowns, most likely due to the demand for privacy that always exists in the industry.

Dogecoin's technical recovery attempt is hitting somewhat of a wall, with daily, weekly and four-hour trends showing a clear bearish dynamic in addition to the price moving below all 8 tracked moving averages on the chart.

As the CoinGlass data suggests, the trading activity we are witnessing today is mixed: spot and futures volumes are descending, with a slight increase in open interest. $584 million in futures volume and $86 million in spot volume. Long and short liquidations are balanced.

Unfortunately, the lack of network activity suggests a baseless price recovery on the market right now: only 37 thousand addresses were active in the last 24 hours, a 24% decrease YTD. Additionally, explorer data suggests that the ten largest DOGE addresses hold more than 44% of the token's available supply.

It doesn't suggest that only 10 users hold a large part of the token's supply, but rather a high concentration of DOGE on exchanges, which quite often prompts additional selling pressure.

Sources indicate that with the low volume and open interest, any technical price level, both resistance and support, can get invalidated swiftly; however, highlighting them could be useful. The first resistance rests at $0.0599, with a trend recovery threshold located around $0.06.

Sources indicate that support levels lie all the way down to the important psychological level of $0.05, the nearest being $0.054. The obvious trend reversal threshold is, of course, $0.06. Until the price establishes a foothold above it, discussing a recovery is not the best option out there.

Can Institutions Secretly Buy Billions of XRP? Ripple Veteran Says It Is 'Not Impossible'

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (410 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: U

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ripple’s longtime CTO emeritus David Schwartz does not think institutions can privately snap up billions of XRP via dark pools without affecting the token’s price on public markets.
  • Why wouldn't people generally want the price to rise when they buy?
  • This was in response to a question posed by an XRP community member wondering if private trading platforms might give institutions an advantage over retail investors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ripple’s longtime CTO emeritus David Schwartz does not think institutions can privately snap up billions of XRP via dark pools without affecting the token’s price on public markets.

"I don't think so. Who are they buying the XRP from? Why wouldn't people generally want the price to rise when they buy? But it's not impossible," Schwartz wrote on X on Nov. 24.

This was in response to a question posed by an XRP community member wondering if private trading platforms might give institutions an advantage over retail investors.

Earlier in the conversation, Schwartz noted the pros and cons of dark pools for retail traders.

Industry observers note that he mentioned one disadvantage: less efficient price discovery. Given that bids and offers are obscured, retail traders in public markets have less insight into other traders’ bids and ask prices.

According to recent reports, if there is a large XRP holder who is already inclined to sell at the current price, an institution could arrange a private trade with this holder without needing to place a massive buy order on an exchange. They could execute the trade without driving the public price up as they buy.

According to recent reports, however, will there be enough sellers interested in offloading billions of XRP like this? One might run out of sellers willing to sell at that price. So, the buyer might need to up the ante to find the next willing seller.

A dark pool can hide order size, but one still needs someone on the other side to execute that order.

Plus, a buyer will naturally prefer not to tip its hand while accumulating a position.

Schwartz left open the possibility of a private purchase at scale, but the possibility is rather low.

Sources indicate that when asked why XRP Ledger developments were not doing anything for XRP’s price on Nov. 9, Schwartz pointed to the broader crypto market.

He also debunked the notion that Ripple had some secret initiative it was not sharing with holders. The manufacturer regularly talks about its intends.

Schwartz also mentioned a practical benefit of XRP being worth more in the: a higher price could mean cheaper liquidity provision and less slippage (the difference between the expected price a trader pays and the price they actually pay).

At the same time, he was less convinced that demand for XRP to pay transaction fees could have a big impact on the price by itself.

Ethereum Foundation Sounds Alarm Over AI Threats

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (400 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: U

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Ethereum Foundation has been working for years to secure the network against a future in which quantum computing breaks the cryptography underpinning Ethereum, but it is now facing a upcoming and more immediate concern around artificial intelligence.
  • AI is identifying bugs in live software more quickly than human reviewers can keep up with, and the Ethereum Foundation has now doubled the size of its protocol security team, according to a recent announcement.
  • As Kev Wedderburn wrote in a post from Devcon, AI models are now identifying thousands of bugs in the Linux kernel, one of the most scrutinized codebases in the world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Ethereum Foundation has been working for years to secure the network against a future in which quantum computing breaks the cryptography underpinning Ethereum, but it is now facing a upcoming and more immediate concern around artificial intelligence.

AI is identifying bugs in live software more quickly than human reviewers can keep up with, and the Ethereum Foundation has now doubled the size of its protocol security team, according to a recent announcement.

As Kev Wedderburn wrote in a post from Devcon, AI models are now identifying thousands of bugs in the Linux kernel, one of the most scrutinized codebases in the world.

For Ethereum developers, the immediate challenge is ensuring that bugs are not present in their software before an upgrade.

The longer-term challenge is mathematical. Ethereum uses digital signatures to identify who can spend funds and which validators have approved the state of the chain.

Wedderburn says that AI's advances in analyzing decades-old algorithms raise questions about the mathematical assumptions underlying those signatures that researchers should consider.

Industry observers note that it is not clear whether AI could break Ethereum's existing cryptography. However,  the Ethereum Foundation wants work on new cryptography to be underway.

After more than a year of considering various signature schemes, the Ethereum Foundation has decided to replace elliptic-curve signatures with hash-based cryptography.

The argument is that Ethereum already relies on cryptographic hash security, and by using hashes for signatures too, it can remove an additional assumption about the difficulty of solving mathematical problems associated with elliptic curves.

The proposal affects three areas of Ethereum.

It would see validators use hash-based keys for their signatures, which in turn changes how block finality is determined on the network.

Wallet developers would need to provide people with a way to transition their accounts to hash-based signatures.

And Ethereum's change to the cryptography used for commitments to data (blobs) that rollups publish to the network would require adjustments from rollups too.

According to recent reports, one challenge is the size of the signatures. Hash-based signatures are much larger, so developers need to consider how that affects the hardware needed to run a node at home.

Staking pools and multisig wallets would need adjustments too. So would smart contracts that rely on existing cryptography.

There will also be a need to adjust tools that rely on the signature scheme currently used by Ethereum validators (BLS).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Crypto exchange Kraken recently faced a flash crash that was caused by a liquidity shortage in one of its Canadian-dollar trading markets, rather than an actual crash in Bitcoin [BTC]’s global market price.
  • Over the weekend, Bitcoin’s price on Kraken’s BTC/CAD trading pair suddenly dropped to C$24,250.
  • This came as a shock because Bitcoin was trading around $57,650 on Kraken’s BTC/USD market during that period.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crypto exchange Kraken recently faced a flash crash that was caused by a liquidity shortage in one of its Canadian-dollar trading markets, rather than an actual crash in Bitcoin [BTC]’s global market price.

Over the weekend, Bitcoin’s price on Kraken’s BTC/CAD trading pair suddenly dropped to C$24,250. This was equivalent to approximately $16,900 at the prevailing USD/CAD exchange rate.

This came as a shock because Bitcoin was trading around $57,650 on Kraken’s BTC/USD market during that period. In Bitcoin trading at nearly 70% below its price on other markets.

However, this was not a market-wide Bitcoin crash, as other major exchanges continued to show Bitcoin trading between $55,000 and $60,000.

The primary suspected reason was a sudden shortage of liquidity in Kraken’s BTC/CAD order book. This liquidity shortage, aka liquidity vacuum, is what caused a sudden price crash without Bitcoin’s actual market value declining.

Expressing their opinion on the matter, Blockstream CEO Adam Back suggested that the disruption may have originated from a market maker running out of funds in Kraken’s USD/CAD market.

As expected, this distortion may have spread to other CAD trading pairs through arbitrage, where traders buy assets at lower prices and sell them elsewhere at higher prices.

It has been revealed that however, Kraken has not confirmed this explanation, yet. The exchange maintained that all orders were processed correctly and refused to reverse completed trades.

This followed the exchange experiencing a one-hour technical outage on 30 October 2026, affecting its website, app, and trading APIs.

But at the same time, Kraken recently expanded its xStocks platform to over 1,000 tokenized stock listings, according to AMBCrypto’s previous report.

Shiba Inu (SHIB) community members have debuted a new block explorer for Shibarium, the layer-2 network of the SHIB ecosystem, and Shiba Inu lead Shytoshi Kusama has remained silent on X since May.

Recent findings suggest that shiba Inu community veteran Mazrael revealed the latest explorer, scan.shibfun.app, in an X post. "Shibarium has a new block explorer," he wrote. According to Mazrael, the explorer was "built by the community, powered by ShibWatch, dressed in the Eternity Hub look.".

It has been revealed that the launch comes as SHIB trades near its lowest levels in years. In November, the price of SHIB fell as low as $0.00000337, its lowest level since 2021, and on Nov. 22, the token traded at around $0.00000362, according to CoinMarketCap.

It has been revealed that according to the post, owners can type a .shib name in the search bar and land on the wallet linked to it, and the explorer also shows newly introduced Shiboshis from Shibarium every day. For developers, Mazrael listed contract verification, read and write functions for contracts, the activity of ERC-4337 smart wallets, and a free API, which he described as "Etherscan-style too." Method names are decoded as well, and in Mazrael's words, there are "no more mystery 0x codes." The explorer also has a DApps page with Shibarium games and apps, and a button that adds Shibarium to a wallet in one click.

In a recent development, the work on the explorer is not finished yet. "Live blocks are complete now, and older history indexing," Mazrael wrote. On Tuesday, the explorer itself showed that 3% of Shibarium blocks had been indexed, and a notice on the site said that some of the counts may be inaccurate. Mazrael added that the fresh explorer can be found on Shib.io under ShibWatch.

Shytoshi Kusama's last post or interaction on X dates back to May 13, 2026. In September, Kusama changed his X bio to "Polish" and his location to "Close," and he has not explained the meaning of either word. The official Shibarium account on X has not posted since July 13, 2026.

It has been revealed that still, Shibarium updates kept coming from community members. In October, Mazrael remarked that CreateX, a standard factory for deploying contracts at the same address on different chains, went live on Shibarium. According to Mazrael, all 12 Safe v1.4.1 contracts were deployed to their canonical addresses through the Safe Singleton Factory, and x402 went live too, so AI agents can now pay in SHIB, TREAT and wrapped BONE.

In September 2025, attackers exploited the Shibarium bridge and withdrew about $2.4 million worth of assets from it.

According to Shibariumscan, Shibarium processed 546 transactions in a single day in late November, and on Oct. 31, the daily number of transactions on the network was 6,370. Since its launch in August 2023, Shibarium has processed more than 1.5 billion transactions in total.

Sources indicate that at the same time, the number of SHIB holders on Ethereum passed 1.7 million on Nov. 17, according to Etherscan.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that the PV5 is Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business.
  • So far, the PV5 has mostly been available in Passenger and Cargo body styles with several different variations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kia opened orders for two new PV5 electric van variants, the PV5 Chassis and PV5 Cargo L2/H2, in the UK.

It has been revealed that the PV5 is Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business. Built on Hyundai Motor’s dedicated modular skateboard platform, E-GMP.S, Kia can easily swap body styles to enable “limitless possibilities.”.

So far, the PV5 has mostly been available in Passenger and Cargo body styles with several different variations.

Kia added the PV5 Chassis, an open-bed model that can be converted into just about anything. In the UK, Kia is offering conversions through TGS Automotive Group, including lightweight tipper, Dropside, and Box solutions.

The PV5 Chassis is available exclusively with the long-range 71.2 kWh battery in the UK, which Kia said could offer a potential WLTP range of up to 258 miles (416 km).

For reference, the PV5 Cargo L2/H1, which uses the same 71.2 kWh battery, offers a WLTP range of up to 258 miles (416 km). Other markets will also have a standard-range 51.1 kWh option.

The Chassis model is 4,610 mm long, 1,895 mm wide, and 1,935 mm tall, with a 2,995 mm wheelbase.

Its compact size and 5.5-meter turning radius, Kia remarked, make it easy to maneuver in city streets, construction sites, and other tight work areas.

Industry observers note that inside, the PV5 Chassis features two seats. Like other variants, it includes a 12.9″ navigation screen and a 7.5″ driver display with standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

The Chassis model supports DC fast charging up to 120 kW, enabling the battery to charge from 10% to 80% in about 30 minutes. Using an 11 kW AC supply, it takes about 6 hours and 30 minutes to charge from 10% to 100%.

In a recent development, payload depends on the configuration. Kia noted the Dropside offers a payload of up to 633 kg, while the Tipper can carry 561 kg.

In the UK, the PV5 Chassis is now on sale from £32,916 ($43,400) on the road, including the expected £5,000 ($6,700) UK Zero Emission Van Grant.

According to recent reports, however, it’s an “incomplete vehicle,” as Kia describes it. The converted PV5 Dropside is priced from £40,110 ($53,500) on the road, including the ZEVG, while the PV5 Tipper starts at £41,310 ($55,000).

Recent findings suggest that kia also rolled out the larger PV5 Cargo L2/H2 in the UK. The newly introduced variant is 4,695mm long, 1,895mm wide, and 2,200mm high, with a 2,995mm wheelbase.

According to recent reports, the taller roof opens up an internal cargo-area height of 1,815mm. It also offers a greater load capacity than the L1/H1 and L2/H2, with 5.2 cubic meters.

In a recent development, it’s available in three- and four-door configurations with the choice of two or three seats. The three-door versions have a maximum payload of 630 kg, while the four-door models have dual sliding doors and offer a payload of up to 600 kg. Both versions can tow up to 1,500 kg.

Like the Chassis model, the PV5 Cargo L2/H2 is available in the UK exclusively with the 71.2 kWh battery, which provides a WLTP range of up to 239 miles.

Inside, it features the same setup as the other PV5 variants, including a 12.9″ touchscreen navigation screen and a 7.5″ driver display.

The base PV5 Cargo L2/H2 Essential two-seat starts at £35,016 ($46,700), on the road, including ZEVG.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Spot Bitcoin [BTC] ETFs have been facing a tough time thanks to consecutive days of outflows.
  • That said, in 2026, it was only in the months of August, September, and April that Bitcoin ETFs attracted $3.52 billion, $2.65 billion, and $1.97 billion in inflows, respectively.
  • On the contrary, the month of June recorded $4.51 billion in outflows, while May saw $2.43 billion leave these investment products.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spot Bitcoin [BTC] ETFs have been facing a tough time thanks to consecutive days of outflows. According to SoSo Value data, U.S Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $669 million in net outflows on 20th November, marking their fourth consecutive day of outflows.

That said, in 2026, it was only in the months of August, September, and April that Bitcoin ETFs attracted $3.52 billion, $2.65 billion, and $1.97 billion in inflows, respectively.

On the contrary, the month of June recorded $4.51 billion in outflows, while May saw $2.43 billion leave these investment products. November has recorded approximately $4.14 billion in net outflows so far.

According to recent reports, november flows in Bitcoin Spot ETFs have swung sharply across the three years. For instance, November 2024 was the strongest, with net inflows of about $6.49 billion during the post-election rally, lifting cumulative inflows from $24.2 billion to $30.7 billion. However, November 2025 reversed to net outflows of 3.48 billion, while November 2026 has so far been worse. That hinted at a swing of roughly $10.6 billion from Nov 2024 to Nov 2026.

Glassnode’s analysis also pointed out this trend that Bitcoin ETF trading volume has fallen below its median since launch, indicating reduced market participation and interest.

Combined with sustained outflows, this alluded to weakening investor demand. However, lower volume can also reflect reduced speculative activity rather than outright bearish sentiment.

However, at times, periods of low interest and reduced market participation can offer better accumulation opportunities than periods of excessive excitement.

Here, it’s worth pointing out that these netflows coincided with BTC’s price trading close to $61,330 at press time, after a drop of 24% over the past month.

At the same time, Bitcoin has recorded several negative netflow readings throughout November, with the latest reading at around -1.1K BTC. In other words, more Bitcoin may be leaving exchanges than entering them. While this can reduce potential selling pressure on exchanges, it does not necessarily confirm accumulation.

Meanwhile, the Bitcoin Spot Volume Bubble Map revealed a noticeable change in market activity, with trading activity not particularly overheated during the price decline.

However, with recent readings showing some heating signs as the price approached the $60,000-level, caution will be useful.
