📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toyota and Subaru’s fresh electric SUVs are catching on with buyers, offering various options and prices ranging from about $35,000 to $45,000, or the “sweet spot” of the US market.

The US electric vehicle market rebounded in the third quarter with 262,649 EVs sold, according to Kelley Blue Book estimates, up 6.1% from Q2 and the strongest performance of the year.

Although nearly every automaker has sold fewer EVs so far this year than in the same period in 2025, as buyers rushed to claim the $7,500 tax credit before it expired, a handful of brands are seeing considerably higher demand.

Outside of Rivian, Toyota and Subaru are the only brands that have higher year-over-year EV sales in the US through the third quarter.

Combined, Toyota and Subaru have sold nearly 50,000 EVs through the first nine months of 2026, more than double compared to the same period last year.

Toyota alone has sold nearly 35,000 electric vehicles, up 183.4% YOY, while Subaru sold 14,630, up 46.7%. And that’s not even including the additional 12,676 sold under the Lexus brand, up 137.4% YOY.

While the two Japanese automakers were infamously slow to transition to battery electric vehicles, the timing worked in their favor.

Recent findings suggest that after launching the heavily updated bZ in late 2025, previously called the bZ4X, Toyota’s electric SUV suddenly became one of America’s most popular EVs. Through Q3, it was the fourth best-selling EV in the US, trailing only the Hyundai IONIQ 5, Tesla Model 3, and Tesla Model Y.

In a recent development, starting at $35,000, the Toyota bZ is one of the most affordable EVs in the US. It also offers up to 314 miles of range in the FWD Plus trim, which starts at $37,980.

Toyota and Subaru now each sell three electric SUVs, which share the same platform and technology.

With prices ranging from roughly $35,000 to about $45,000, Stephanie Valdez Streaty, director of industry insights at Cox Automotive, mentioned (via Bloomberg) Toyota and Subaru’s new EVs are affordable and hit the “sweet spot” of the US car market.

Toyota also sells the smaller, sporty C-HR, starting at $37,080, and the larger, more rugged bZ Woodland, which starts at $45,380.

Subaru, on the other hand, sells the updated Solterra ($38,495, plus the smaller Uncharted ($34,995) and midsize Trailseeker ($39,995).

Karla Fisher, a Marine and retired engineer, told Bloomberg that the Subaru Trailseeker was her “most favorite car of all time.”.

Recent findings suggest that while she considered buying an EV before the $7,500 federal credit expired last September, none met her requirements at the time. Fisher wanted at least 7″ of ground clearance, 250 miles or more range, and a price that was similar, or even less than a comparible gas-powered vehicle.

Sources indicate that the Subaru Trailseeker offers all of that and starts at under $40,000. Toyota and Subaru’s electric SUVs all start at about $45,000 or less, which is even less than the average new vehicle.

According to the latest Kelley Blue Book figures, the average price for a latest vehicle in the US reached a record $51,109 in October, up 2.1% YOY.

Great as these may be, there is little inventory to be found.

There are less than 500 Uncharted available Nationwide.

You can't sell what you don't have. Yes, they can be ordered for sure, but how many missed sales does that model create?

Industry observers note that subaru spokesperson Dominick Infante noted the affordable EV prices are mainly thanks to its partnership with Toyota. “We do believe there’s an EV future,” Infante added.

Next year, both brands will add a three-row electric SUV with the Toyota Highlander EV and Subaru Getaway.

Source: Glassnode — BTC Market Pulse, Nov. 23.

DWF Labs counted over $4.9 billion in crypto-wide liquidations in the week to Nov. 22, including $3.75 billion in longs, about 76%.

It has been revealed that the prior week brought nearly $5.8 billion, so roughly $10.7 billion cleared in two weeks. Fewer leveraged positions mean a falling price has less collateral to wipe out. Options traders continue to pay up for protection, as the 25-delta skew rose to 17.4% from 14.4%, its highest since mid-July.

Glassnode's ratio compares short-term-holder supply with long-term-holder supply, a different measure from short-term holders' share of all coins.

Industry observers note that the firm classifies entities by average coin age, with a smoothed transition around 155 days, so the ratio can rise as long-term supply falls, as short-term supply grows, or both. A 0.5-point rise is modest, but it arrived while prices fell and futures positions shrank.

Profitable supply fell 6.9%. Both readings come from Glassnode's Nov. 23 report and are rounded to one decimal place.

Source: Glassnode — BTC Market Pulse, Nov. 23.

Supply in profit dropped from 54.2% to 47.3%, leaving 52.7% of circulating supply at a loss or near breakeven.

Short-term-holder net unrealized profit and loss sits at negative 18.3%, its lowest since mid-June. Realized capitalization contracted 0.93% over the month, against 0.06% a week earlier, its weakest reading since July.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs lost about $1.7 billion in the week, the heaviest outflow since early July, and Glassnode puts ETF MVRV at 0.97, which places the average ETF holder below estimated cost basis.

Glassnode's Nov. 17 report supplied the $62,000 to $66,000 cluster where many recent buyers entered, the $74,100 short-term-holder cost basis, the $58,500 June low and the $53,700 realized price as key levels.

From a price near $63,000, $74,100 sits 17.6% higher and $53,700 sits 14.8% lower.

If Bitcoin holds the $62,000 to $66,000 cluster while spot CVD turns positive, ETF outflows reverse, and realized capitalization climbs toward zero, the derivatives reset becomes the base for accumulation.

A move toward $74,100 would then test whether recent buyers can reach breakeven and avoid a rush to sell, while futures positions rebuild gradually behind spot buying.

If Bitcoin fails to hold that cluster while ETF outflows continue and realized capitalization keeps contracting, sellers are holders closing losses, and thin futures positioning offers little cushion.

A break below $58,500 would put the $53,700 realized price in view, and both paths are conditional scenarios built on Glassnode's reference levels.

The derivatives half of the reset is complete, while the spot half awaits evidence of buyers large enough to absorb coins that holders sell at a loss.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Strive (Nasdaq: ASST) bought no bitcoin last week and sold no stock to fund new purchases, leaving its holdings unchanged at 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday 8-K filing.
  • The Dallas-based manufacturer reported that its bitcoin count was unchanged between Nov.
  • Recent findings suggest that the pause follows a slowdown from the October sprint that built the stack.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Strive (Nasdaq: ASST) bought no bitcoin last week and sold no stock to fund new purchases, leaving its holdings unchanged at 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday 8-K filing.

The Dallas-based manufacturer reported that its bitcoin count was unchanged between Nov. 13 and Nov. 20. It sold no Class A common shares, no SATA preferred shares and no SATS preferred shares in its at-the-market programs from the Nov. 13 close through the Nov. 20 close.

Recent findings suggest that the pause follows a slowdown from the October sprint that built the stack. Strive bought 251 bitcoin for $17.5 million the prior week at an average of $69,853 per coin, after adding just 29 coins the week before that.

Industry observers note that bitcoin traded near $61,000 on Coinbase on Monday afternoon. That is about 12.6% below the $69,853 average Strive paid for its most recent purchase. At that price, the 43,404-coin stack is worth roughly $2.65 billion.

According to recent reports, the filing gives no reason for the pause, and the firm has not said whether it plans to resume weekly buying. Strive has typically disclosed its holdings on Mondays, so next week’s update will show whether the stack grows again.

Most of the stack was built promptly. Strive held 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 and acquired 15,124 more between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30, including a single 6,182-coin purchase. The firm closed a registered offering of 7 million SATS shares on Oct. 20 for about $609 million in net proceeds, which funded much of that run.

Strive’s cash and cash equivalents slipped to $462.4 million as of Nov. 20 from $465.3 million a week earlier, a decline of $2.9 million. The filing does not break out what drove the change.

In a recent development, the manufacturer also still holds 505,000 shares of Strategy’s variable-rate STRC preferred stock. The fair value of that position fell to $47.3 million from $50.5 million, a drop of about $3.2 million, with the share count unchanged.

Industry observers note that share counts were also flat. Strive reported 118,133,002 Class A shares and 9,198,107 Class B shares, for 127,331,109 effective common shares. Outstanding preferred stood at 14,030,176 shares of SATA and 7,141,037 shares of SATS, the 15% perpetual preferred it has used to fund most of its purchases.

In a recent development, strive’s holdings rose from 43,153 bitcoin on Nov. 6 to 43,404 on Nov. 13, and the filing shows no change since. With no common or preferred stock sold, the firm raised no latest capital through its offering programs last week, which left cash as its main resource for dividends and operations.

Strive shares were trading near $15.55 at 3:56 p.m. ET on Monday, up about 7.1% from Friday’s close of $14.51, according to Yahoo Finance. The stock opened near $17.64, a gain of more than 20%, and gave back much of it through the session.

Recent findings suggest that the swing tracked bitcoin-linked stocks broadly after Nvidia reinstated CEO Jensen Huang and sent equities sharply higher, a move Bitcoin Magazine covered earlier Monday. Bitcoin spiked above $64,000 in the morning before sliding back toward $61,000 during U.S. trading hours.

Sources indicate that the stock has lost much of its October run. ASST closed at $30.75 on Oct. 21, so Monday’s price is about 49% lower. It is still roughly 5% above its 2025 year-end close of $14.76.

Strive’s preferred stocks remain a central part of its model. On Nov. 12, the board raised the SATA dividend rate to 13.25% for periods beginning Dec. 1, while SATS continues to pay 15%. Both pay daily cash dividends, so the tech giant’s cash balance funds a steady outflow even in weeks without purchases.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $61,000.

Bubblemaps counted 16 accounts with five funded wallets on Nov. 16 and 11 funded on Nov. 23. Each account started trading within about six minutes of funding and traded exclusively in Nvidia-related markets.

Bubblemaps attributed the $350,000 to all 16 accounts combined, which leaves the Nov. 23 group's share undetermined, and both totals carry its rounding.

Its Kalshi examples, a candidate trading on his own election and a video editor trading on unpublished YouTube content, each involved an identifiable source. Applied to Nvidia, the standard would require evidence that an account operator received the board's decision through an improper disclosure or held a duty to protect it.

Industry observers note that if wallet-level reconstruction ties the 11 Nov. 23 accounts to nothing beyond Trump's endorsement and the campaign behind it, the profits become an example of cheap contracts rewarding an aggressive reading of public information.

A hypothetical trader who set the odds at 10% and bought at 3 cents would expect about a 233% return before costs, while still losing most of the time.

It has been revealed that if on-chain researchers link even one account to improperly disclosed knowledge of the board's decision, that account's trades would fall under the CFTC's standard. The other accounts could sit on the public-information side of the line.

According to recent reports, trump's post gives the 11 Nov. 23 accounts a plausible public explanation. The five accounts funded a week earlier need another one, and the hour of the board vote would show whether the decision existed before Trump posted.

The unresolved issue is whether these traders read public information better than the market or held information the broader market lacked.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The bitcoin price slipped back to near $60,000 early Tuesday, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data, as the Nvidia-fueled rally in stocks cooled and spot bitcoin ETFs posted another heavy day of outflows.
  • Bitcoin faded to near $61,100 on Monday afternoon after spiking as high as $64,500 on Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO.
  • Industry observers note that monday’s ETF figure was the number traders were watching, and it came back negative.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The bitcoin price slipped back to near $60,000 early Tuesday, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data, as the Nvidia-fueled rally in stocks cooled and spot bitcoin ETFs posted another heavy day of outflows.

Bitcoin faded to near $61,100 on Monday afternoon after spiking as high as $64,500 on Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO. The slide continued overnight. Bitcoin fell below $60,000 and touched about $59,400 before edging back to the $60,000 line ahead of the U.S. open. The bitcoin price is now down about 7% from Monday’s high, and it remains less than $5,000 above last week’s two-year low near $55,100.

Industry observers note that monday’s ETF figure was the number traders were watching, and it came back negative. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs shed about $569.7 million on Monday. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $509.3 million of that, while Fidelity’s FBTC was the only fund to take in money, adding $13.3 million.

Industry observers note that it was the fifth straight day of outflows. November’s withdrawals now total about $4.71 billion, topping June’s $4.5 billion record for the worst month since the funds launched in January 2024.

It has been revealed that adam Haeems, head of asset management at Tesseract Group, had called Monday’s flow figure “the first real test of this bounce.” The pattern he flagged, with bitcoin falling during U.S. hours in step with ETF outflows, held again on Monday, and the bitcoin price has given back almost all of Monday’s gains.

Recent findings suggest that wall Street is also giving back some ground. Dow futures fell 0.5%, S&P 500 futures declined 1% and Nasdaq-100 futures dropped 2% early Tuesday. Nvidia (NVDA) slid about 5% in premarket trading after closing up 31.5% at $165.05 on Monday.

It has been revealed that monday’s rally was the strongest day for both the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq since April 2025. The S&P 500 gained 4.7% and the Nasdaq Composite closed 6.5% higher, even as bitcoin failed to hold its own spike.

“With Jensen’s return, it assures people massively,” Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at IG Group, told Reuters. “But it then opens up a whole list of questions that may not be answered very promptly.”.

Rates remain a headwind for the bitcoin price. Newly introduced York Fed President John Williams noted Monday that “there is still work to do” to bring inflation back to the Fed’s 2% target. Markets are fully pricing in a quarter-point hike from the current 3.75% to 4% range when the Fed meets Dec. 8-9.

It has been revealed that treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has pushed back on a bigger hike, but traders still see about a 5% chance of a half-point move. The dollar index is hovering just below a 20-month high, and Wednesday’s PCE inflation report is the last major data point before the December decision.

In a recent development, bitcoin-linked shares are retreating with the coin. Strategy (MSTR) dropped 3.2% in premarket trading after Monness, Crespi, Hardt & Co. cut its price target to $59 from $65, the lowest on Wall Street. Analyst Gus Galá kept a sell rating and projects bitcoin will trade around $50,000.

It has been revealed that that would sit well below the $75,446 average cost Strategy has paid for its 851,305 bitcoin, which it grew by 457 BTC last week. MSCI is also set to remove Strategy from its indexes on Nov. 30, which could force the sale of about 13 million shares. “The premium is gone, and we think a discount can persist,” Galá wrote.

Sources indicate that coinbase (COIN) fell about 3.5% to near $105 before the bell, and miner IREN slipped 4%. Traders will watch whether bitcoin can hold $60,000 through the U.S. session as consumer confidence data lands Tuesday.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $60,000.

Latest Update: Bitcoin developers propose fix for transaction verification gap affecting Lightning wallets

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (704 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cryptoslate

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bitcoin developers have proposed a new verification system that would allow lightweight wallets to independently authenticate transaction signatures recorded on the blockchain.
  • It has been revealed that the draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposal, submitted by developer Jean Pablo on Nov.
  • The proposal could particularly benefit wallets such as Electrum, which supports Bitcoin's Lightning Network and relies on external servers for some blockchain information.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin developers have proposed a new verification system that would allow lightweight wallets to independently authenticate transaction signatures recorded on the blockchain.

It has been revealed that the draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposal, submitted by developer Jean Pablo on Nov. 22, addresses a limitation in how wallets verify transaction information received from external servers.

The proposal could particularly benefit wallets such as Electrum, which supports Bitcoin's Lightning Network and relies on external servers for some blockchain information.

Right now, lightweight wallets can verify that a transaction was included in a Bitcoin block using a cryptographic proof tied to its transaction ID, or txid.

However, that identifier excludes witness data, which contains signatures and other information used to authorize spending under Bitcoin's Segregated Witness (SegWit) system.

Consequently, a wallet could successfully verify a transaction's inclusion while holding witness data that differs from what miners actually included in the block.

Pablo's proposal addresses this discrepancy by introducing standardized witness transaction inclusion proofs built around a second identifier, known as the witness transaction ID, or wtxid.

Unlike the conventional transaction ID, the wtxid incorporates witness data, allowing wallets to verify that the full transaction they received matches the version included in a mined block.

In a recent development, the proposed system connects that identifier to Bitcoin's existing witness commitment, which is recorded in the block's coinbase transaction. A second cryptographic proof then connects the coinbase transaction to the block header.

In a recent development, an ordinary proof checks the transaction ID. The draft adds a path from the witness data to the same block header.

A wallet can compare the witness data it received with what a valid block committed to.

According to recent reports, the proposed path assumes a valid block with a SegWit witness commitment. Chain selection and confirmation depth are separate from inclusion verification.

The diagram follows the two proof paths described in the draft and the wallet verification flow in the Bitcoin Core discussion.

Sources indicate that the proposed path assumes a valid block with a SegWit witness commitment. Chain selection and confirmation depth are separate from inclusion verification.

Together, these checks allow wallets to authenticate witness data without downloading and examining the entire block.

The development follows an earlier request from Electrum contributor SomberNight, who sought witness inclusion proofs to strengthen transaction verification for the wallet's Lightning Network functionality.

Lightning wallets interact with Bitcoin's underlying blockchain when opening, closing and monitoring payment channels, making reliable transaction information particularly important.

The proposed verification system would allow such wallets to independently confirm the witness data supplied by servers while continuing to operate without storing complete blockchain data.

The request previously prompted work on Bitcoin Core, where developers explored extending existing transaction proof commands to cover witness information.

That pull request closed in May without being merged, and developer Sjors Provoost later continued the effort through a separate implementation that introduced commands to generate and verify witness proofs.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin Knots introduced experimental witness-proof support in version 29.1, and Electrum developers have been working on related protocol changes.

However, these efforts use different proof formats, creating compatibility challenges between wallets and the servers providing blockchain information.

Pablo's proposal attempts to resolve those differences by specifying two binary formats and a JSON representation for exchanging and verifying proofs.

The first format provides a separate cryptographic proof for each transaction, while the second reduces duplicated information when verifying multiple transactions together.

In one example involving 10 transactions, the second format reduced proof data from 4,523 bytes to 3,325 bytes, approximately a 26% reduction.

The proposal also includes a Python reference implementation and 93 test cases designed to establish consistent verification behavior across software implementations.

Of those tests, 31 cover proofs that should be accepted, while 62 cover invalid proofs that verification software must reject.

The specification would give Bitcoin Core, Electrum and other wallet developers a common framework for implementing witness verification.

Pablo has requested feedback on the proposed formats and verification requirements, leaving developers to determine whether a shared standard can replace the experimental approaches already in use.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hyundai’s US electric vehicle lineup will look a bit different in 2027, including the latest IONIQ 6 N, a new range-topping IONIQ 9 trim, and a handful of minor updates to the IONIQ 5.

Hyundai revealed its 2027 model-year changes on Wednesday, including the new IONIQ 6 N and a few slight changes to the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9.

While Hyundai discontinued the standard IONIQ 6, it added the high-performance IONIQ 6 N for the 2027 lineup.

In a recent development, the IONIQ 6 N is Hyundai’s second performance EV, following the IONIQ 5 N. Powered by a dual-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain, the electric sports car delivers a combined 641 hp and 568 lb-ft of torque.

Hyundai noted the IONIQ 6 N can sprint from 0 to 60 mph in 3.2 seconds, beating the IONIQ 5 N at 3.25 seconds.

Like the IONIQ 5 N, it also includes fun added features, like N e-Shift and an N Active Sound+ system that simulates the sounds and sensations of a traditional gas-powered sports car with an 8-speed dual-clutch transmission.

It uses an 84 kWh battery that provides up to 245 miles of pure electric driving range. Thanks to its 800V ultra-fast charging architecture, the IONIQ 6 N can charge from 10% to 80% in about 18 minutes using a 350 kW DC fast charger.

Like Hyundai’s other electric vehicles, it comes standard with a native NACS charging port and a CCS adapter.

The 2027 IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9 are mostly carryover models with a few minor changes, while the IONIQ 5 N remains the same as the 2026 model year.

Changes to the IONIQ 5 for the 2027 model year include roof rails, which are now available on the SEL trim and above; previously, they were only available on the XRT and Limited trims.

Hyundai HomeLink will be available exclusively on the Limited trim, rather than SEL and above, in the current 2026 model year, while the Cargo Cover will be offered as an Accessory only.

Regarding color options, the Gravity Gold Matte and Sage Silver Matte will no longer be available for the 2027 IONIQ 5.

The 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 starts at $35,250, making it one of the most affordable EVs in the US.

In a recent development, that’s for the standard-range IONIQ 5 SE with an EPA-estimated range of up to 245 miles. The extended-range SE RWD model is $2,500 more, starting at $37,750, and offers up to 318 miles of range.

Hyundai’s three-row SUV also received a handful of updates. The 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 9 will be available with a latest Calligraphy Black Ink trim, while the Calligraphy Design will no longer be offered.

Sources indicate that the 2027 IONIQ 9 Calligraphy and Calligraphy Black Ink trims gain a Virtual Gear Shift and heated third-row seats. All variants also gain a Tailgate Emergency Lamp.

In a recent development, on the one hand... the Ioniq5 is due for an update. On the other... I still absolutely love the way it looks, and notice just about every one I pass on the road.

Hyundai has yet to announce prices for the 2027 model. The base 2026 IONIQ 9 S starts at $58,995 and offers an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 335 miles.

The previous top-spec Performance Calligraphy Design AWD started at $76,490, so you can expect the new Calligraphy Black Ink to be around the same, if not even more.

U.S. junk-bond yields rose to 8.46% at the Nov. 20 close as investment-grade yields fell, according to ICE BofA data published Nov. 23 by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Bond investors demanded a bigger premium to own the weakest corporate debt. That gives Bitcoin buyers a separate gauge of risk appetite after Monday's rebound lost momentum.

The yield on the U.S. high-yield index rose from 8.25% on Nov. 16 to 8.46% on Nov. 20. The biggest yield move among the three corporate indexes was in bonds rated CCC or lower. Its effective yield rose from 17.88% to 18.61%.

Over the same dates, the investment-grade corporate yield fell from 5.95% to 5.84%. The two-year Treasury yield fell from 4.83% to 4.63%.

The option-adjusted spread for bonds rated CCC and lower widened 92 basis points, compared with 42 for high yield overall and 8 for investment grade.

CCC and lower is a subset of the high-yield index. Option-adjusted spreads measure the yield premium over the Treasury curve after accounting for embedded options.

Tesla confirms rare new delivery of 50 Semi electric trucks in Chicago

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1059 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla has confirmed a latest batch of Tesla Semi deliveries, with its official Semi account saying today that “Chicago’s first 50 Semis” are on their way to the city.
  • Tesla doesn’t disclose Semi deliveries, and it claims its fresh Nevada factory can build 50,000 of them a year.
  • The post, published on the @tesla_semi account on X at noon ET today, shows four Semis lined up at sunset under the caption “Hello Windy City.” Tesla didn’t name the customer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla has confirmed a latest batch of Tesla Semi deliveries, with its official Semi account saying today that “Chicago’s first 50 Semis” are on their way to the city.

It’s a rare data point. Tesla doesn’t disclose Semi deliveries, and it claims its fresh Nevada factory can build 50,000 of them a year.

The post, published on the @tesla_semi account on X at noon ET today, shows four Semis lined up at sunset under the caption “Hello Windy City.” Tesla didn’t name the customer.

Hello Windy CityChicago’s first 50 Semis en route for delivery pic.twitter.com/75kig8yWsb.

It has been revealed that but the only 50-truck Semi order tied to Chicago belongs to HMD Trucking. The family-owned carrier was founded in Chicago in 1998, runs more than 650 trucks (almost all diesel), and ordered 50 Semis right after Tesla’s production event in September.

Recent findings suggest that HMD took its first truck on November 2 and states it’s the first Tesla Semi registered in Illinois. COO Michael Mahler said Tesla “has been transparent with us regarding the capabilities of Semi every step of the way.”.

It has been revealed that the tech giant ran a Semi for more than 4,000 miles over the summer and averaged 1.74 kWh per mile, right in line with Tesla’s 1.7 kWh/mile claim. The first trucks will mostly handle local runs around Chicago, and HMD is installing its own chargers there since Tesla’s Megacharger network is still concentrated along the I-5 and I-10 corridors in the West.

Owner Henry Malukas told MotorTrend the deal is worth about $15 million. That’s roughly $300,000 per truck, in line with the ~$290,000 Long Range pricing we reported when the first truck came off the high-volume line and a long way from the $180,000 Tesla advertised in 2017.

Here’s the problem: it’s nearly impossible to tell how many Semis Tesla is actually building.

It has been revealed that tesla introduced volume production at its Sparks, Nevada factory on September 24, after pushing the ramp out of 2025. It states the 1.8 million sq ft plant is built for 50,000 trucks a year. But it never gave a ramp schedule, and its quarterly production and delivery reports only count “passenger vehicles sold to customers.” The Semi isn’t in there.

In a recent development, so we’re left with proxies. Tesla notes its Semi fleet has over 98% uptime, without saying how major that fleet is. Before this year, the largest Semi fleet was PepsiCo’s, at 86 trucks in 2024. California’s truck voucher program received 965 Semi applications between January 2025 and February 2026, which points to real demand but says nothing about output.

In a recent development, the order book is the other clue. Einride ordered 500 Semis in August, WattEV has 370 on order, IMC Logistics wants 50 for California, and the ZET SCALE alliance picked Tesla as main supplier for 2,500 trucks. And now HMD’s 50 are rolling into Chicago, one of the first Semi fleets that will have to deal with a Midwest winter. Wisconsin’s Paper Transport has also been piloting a Semi in the Chicago market since the summer.

None of that adds up to a production rate, but it does look like Tesla is slowly ramping up deliveries.

Sources indicate that tesla keeps the Semi numbers vague on purpose. It’s happy to talk about a 50,000-truck-a-year factory, and it posts hero shots when a batch ships, but it won’t give the one number that shows whether the factory is anywhere close to that.

According to recent reports, I think the semi is going to be a significant seller but its going to take some time to produce enough of them and for companies to gather enough data. Once the investment is justified, there will be customers and repeat customers. After that, it will only be a matter of time before other electric semi truck manufacturers start popping up with offerings and thats a good thing for everyone.

The 50,000 figure is what makes the Semi look like a real business to investors instead of a niche program that took nine years to get going. Tesla has a long history of quoting capacity long before it reaches it, so we shouldn’t treat “built for 50,000” as anything more than a ceiling.

Our read: Tesla is still far from that 50,000 rate. Fifty trucks for one customer is 0.1% of a year at full capacity, and if Tesla were shipping in large volumes, a single 50-unit batch wouldn’t get its own post. But the ramp has clearly started, the order book is real, and it’s plausible Tesla gets into the thousands by the end of the year.

Good for HMD, too. A 650-truck diesel fleet in a cold market is exactly the kind of customer the Semi has to win. Malukas admitted “we don’t have real numbers yet” on savings, and HMD’s own blog is fairly sober about cost and winter range. Local routes, depot charging and a Chicago winter is the right way to find out. It all sounds plausible for the Tesla Semi.

#178813. Latest Update: Relai Introduces Stacks, Letting Bitcoin Savers Split Intends by Goal

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (529 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Bitcoinmagazine ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Relai Introduces Stacks, Letting Bitcoin Savers Split Intends by Goal

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (529 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Swiss bitcoin app Relai launched Stacks on Tuesday, a feature that lets consumers run several recurring bitcoin savings plans side by side, one for each goal, such as a house, a wedding or a child’s first car.
  • Stacks is live for all Relai consumers in Switzerland and the European Union.
  • According to recent reports, since September, Relai users have been able to change the amount and buy date of an active plan.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Swiss bitcoin app Relai launched Stacks on Tuesday, a feature that lets consumers run several recurring bitcoin savings plans side by side, one for each goal, such as a house, a wedding or a child’s first car.

Stacks is live for all Relai consumers in Switzerland and the European Union. Each Stack carries its own amount and schedule, and users can change either at any time without starting over, the company said. A savings plan is Relai’s version of dollar-cost averaging: buying a fixed amount of bitcoin on a set schedule, weekly or monthly, regardless of price. Savers use it to avoid timing the market.

According to recent reports, since September, Relai users have been able to change the amount and buy date of an active plan. Stacks applies that to several goals at once, so a saver can put more toward a house one month, slow down a car fund the next and leave an emergency reserve untouched.

In practice, Stacks is an organizing layer, not a new account. Relai’s help pages describe each Stack as a separate pot with its own bitcoin address inside the same wallet. People get up to five custom Stacks plus a main balance, and moving bitcoin between them takes a regular on-chain transaction with a network fee.

Relai is self-custodial, meaning it does not hold customers’ bitcoin. The coins in every Stack sit in a wallet controlled by a 12-word recovery phrase, or seed phrase, that only the user has. All Stacks share that one phrase, and restoring the wallet with it brings every Stack back.

The trade-off is responsibility. A saver who loses the phrase and the phone has no password reset and no support desk that can recover the coins. Anyone who gets the phrase can take them, which is why attackers have gone as far as tampering with hardware wallets to capture it.

Recent findings suggest that “Everyone saves for something. A home, their kids, the freedom to stop working one day,” noted Julian Liniger, Relai’s co-founder and CEO. “With Stacks, you can save for each of those goals in Bitcoin, at your own pace.”.

It has been revealed that in the EU, Relai’s French unit is authorized by France’s financial markets regulator, the AMF, as a crypto-asset service provider under MiCA, the bloc’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation. Relai secured that license in October 2025, and under MiCA a firm licensed in one member state can “passport” its services across the bloc.

Swiss and Liechtenstein customers are served by Relai AG, which is affiliated with VQF, a self-regulatory organization recognized by Swiss regulator FINMA under the country’s anti-money laundering law.

According to recent reports, goal-based saving in bitcoin also carries price risk that a bank savings account does not. Bitcoin traded near $60,000 on Tuesday, more than 50% below its record above $126,000 set in October 2025, after falling below $60,000 last week.

Relai, founded in Zurich in 2020, says it has processed more than $1 billion in trading volume. The app charges a standard 1% fee, but each user’s first monthly savings blueprint order of up to 100 Swiss francs or euros is fee-free.

#178810. Latest Update: Tesla extends Cybertruck production to late summer 2027 amid fan backlash

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1083 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Tesla extends Cybertruck production to late summer 2027 amid fan backlash

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1083 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Elon Musk now says Tesla will keep building the Cybertruck “through the end of summer 2027” to “work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog.” That buys the electric pickup roughly two to three more months, five days after Tesla first declared it was killing it.
  • The reprieve lands as a growing number of Tesla’s own fans push back on the decision, and on what it says about Tesla’s future as a organization that sells cars to people.
  • On November 6, Musk said Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas “around the middle of next year” to make room for Cybercab.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk now says Tesla will keep building the Cybertruck “through the end of summer 2027” to “work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog.” That buys the electric pickup roughly two to three more months, five days after Tesla first declared it was killing it.

The reprieve lands as a growing number of Tesla’s own fans push back on the decision, and on what it says about Tesla’s future as a organization that sells cars to people.

On November 6, Musk said Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas “around the middle of next year” to make room for Cybercab. On November 9, he wrote the line would shut “in about 8 months” and that Tesla would “have to return deposits for a lot of people.” Now it’s the end of summer.

In order to work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog, production will be extended through the end of summer 2027.

Industry observers note that the reasons have moved around just as much. First it was factory space, then “a very limited number of smart, dedicated people,” then the “opportunity cost” of the truck’s complexity. We went through each of them: Tesla is ending the Cybertruck as sales stall at about 10% of plan, Musk’s demand claim doesn’t survive the numbers, and Musk admitted Tesla doesn’t have the talent to run more than one vehicle program.

And the “backlog” is one Tesla built itself. Before the announcement, the truck was selling at a pace of roughly 30,000 units a year, about 10% of the 250,000 Tesla planned for, on a line with over 125,000 units of installed capacity. Telling people the truck is going away creates a last-call rush. That’s not demand Tesla was missing before.

Tesla also raised Cybertruck prices by up to 10% the same day and paused orders for the base Dual Motor. The cheapest Cybertruck you can order is now $92,490, up from $69,990 in early August.

Some of the people in that backlog have been waiting a while. Several cheering in Musk’s replies say they’re still waiting on the $59,990 Cybertruck Tesla sold for “10 days only” in February. One asked whether Tesla will prioritize Premium and Cyberbeast orders over theirs. Musk didn’t answer.

The most telling replies weren’t about the truck. Chuck Cook, one of the best-known FSD testers in the Tesla community, quote-tweeted Musk asking him to “change your mind,” adding: “Cybercab won’t haul my bees.”.

Another longtime Tesla supporter, Phil Trubey, asked for “a vehicle roadmap post end of summer 2027,” followed by: “Will Tesla make any other vehicle?”.

That’s the right question, and Tesla hasn’t revealed a single fresh consumer vehicle to answer it. Tesla started 2026 with five consumer vehicle programs: Model S, Model X, Model 3, Model Y, and Cybertruck. It ended Model S and Model X production in the spring, citing “autonomy.” The Cybertruck goes next. By fall 2027, Tesla’s consumer lineup will be the Model 3 and Model Y, two vehicles that launched in 2017 and 2020.

Tesla’s answer to the affordable car it promised for years was stripped-down “Standard” versions of those same two vehicles. In China, its second-biggest market, Tesla turned Giga Shanghai into an export hub, and domestic retail sales crashed 66% in October to the lowest level in over four years.

Even Unplugged Performance, the biggest Tesla tuner around, offered to take the Cybertruck line off Tesla’s hands and pay a license fee. People want this truck built. Tesla doesn’t.

We’ve been warning about this for years, and for years we got called haters for it.

The pattern has been clear since Tesla swapped its affordable car aims for Robotaxi in 2024. No fresh consumer platform. Model S and X killed “for autonomy.” Cybertruck killed “for Cybercab.” A Roadster pitched as a thruster stunt nine years after its unveiling. Every product decision points away from selling cars to people and toward robotaxis and Optimus, two businesses that don’t generate meaningful revenue today.

I am beginning to suspect that Elon does not always tell the truth.

As long as we have an economic climate that allows massive amounts of money to be made off of speculation as opposed to actual product, future bots and robotaxis have a great deal of value whether they actually become viable or not.

A two-to-three-month extension doesn’t change any of that. It’s a gesture to the loudest part of the fan base, and it happens to let Tesla sell a few thousand more trucks at prices up to 10% higher than last week. Fine. But the people who bought into Tesla’s mission to accelerate the world’s transition to sustainable energy are now realizing that mission was quietly rewritten, and the word “sustainable” didn’t make the cut.

Tesla is becoming a company that sells two aging EVs to fund a bet on autonomy. That might work out for shareholders. We have our doubts, given Tesla is still behind Waymo by every public metric. But it’s a lot less exciting for the people who wanted the next great Tesla car.

The question for fans now: when the Model 3 and Model Y get their own “opportunity cost” post on X, will anyone actually be surprised?

If you’re buying an EV, Cybertruck or not, powering it with home solar can cut your fuel costs to nearly zero. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, bisq released a security update for Bisq 2, its peer-to-peer Bitcoin trading software, on Nov.
  • In the 2.1.16 release notes, Bisq identified the flaw as Java4Shell and noted it could let an attacker run code on an affected system.
  • 25 change, Bisq 2 nodes running versions older than 2.1.14 can miss offers and trade messages.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, bisq released a security update for Bisq 2, its peer-to-peer Bitcoin trading software, on Nov. 23 and urged desktop consumers to install version 2.1.16 as soon as possible, even if they have no trade in progress. Version 2.1.16 fixes a flaw in the app’s bundled Java software, and Bisq indicates desktop users need the update to keep trading. A separate network change on Nov. 25 requires nodes to run at least 2.1.14.

In the 2.1.16 release notes, Bisq identified the flaw as Java4Shell and noted it could let an attacker run code on an affected system. The release also includes a Tor security revision.

After the Nov. 25 change, Bisq 2 nodes running versions older than 2.1.14 can miss offers and trade messages. Bisq announced the change in October when it released version 2.1.14. Starting Nov. 25, updated nodes will require newer V2 signatures on the data they store and share. Bisq warns that versions below 2.1.14 will have trouble connecting and exchanging data, and the project will end support for them.

The project's headless node release notes warn that trades can stall if a node on 2.1.13 misses messages it needs to move a deal forward.

The official downloads page lists the desktop builds for Windows, macOS and Linux and provides PGP signatures and a public key for verifying the installers.

It has been revealed that version 2.1.16 also changes how the app handles a trade across a restart. It saves messages that arrive before the trade can process them, then applies them on startup if trading is enabled and the node meets the minimum trading version. In pre-release testing, a Bisq contributor reported completing test trades after upgrading Ubuntu nodes from 2.1.15 to a 2.1.16 release candidate. The test used nodes accessed through the API and covered trades that were already open during the upgrade.

According to recent reports, for mobile traders, the version to check depends on the app. Bisq Easy Mobile runs its own node on Android. Its 0.15.0 release moved to the 2.1.14 core. Bisq notes users still on 0.14.x can miss offers and messages or see trades stall after Nov. 25. Bisq urges users to install Bisq Easy 0.17.0, which uses the 2.1.15 core, to keep trading.

Sources indicate that bisq Connect on Android and iOS controls a separate desktop or headless Bisq 2 node. Users who rely on a node run by someone else need that operator to check the version and upgrade it if it falls below the network minimum.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • BYD is apologizing after a supplier error left some owners of its fresh full-size flagship SUV with the wrong wheels.
  • The Great Tang, or Da Tang as it’s called in China, is the first flagship D-segment SUV under its Dynasty series, the largest and most luxurious SUV from the lineup.
  • After opening preorders at the Beijing Auto Show in April, BYD mentioned the high-end SUV secured over 30,000 preorders in 24 hours.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD is apologizing after a supplier error left some owners of its fresh full-size flagship SUV with the wrong wheels.

The Great Tang, or Da Tang as it’s called in China, is the first flagship D-segment SUV under its Dynasty series, the largest and most luxurious SUV from the lineup.

After opening preorders at the Beijing Auto Show in April, BYD mentioned the high-end SUV secured over 30,000 preorders in 24 hours. Two weeks later, preorders reached over 100,000.

By the time it went on sale in mid-June, over 150,000 buyers had preordered the Great Tang, marking a latest record for a single BYD model.

While it has been the top-selling pure electric large SUV for two months, with more than 10,000 sold since it hit the market, BYD issued an apology on November 11 for fitting the wrong front and rear wheel rims on some Great Tang models.

The apology comes after several owners complained that the wheels were improperly installed on their vehicles.

BYD said the problem stemmed from a coding error by the wheel mesh assembly supplier, which led to incorrect assembly on some Great Tang vehicles.

According to recent reports, the manufacturer stated it “immediately” launched an investigation and corrected the issue so newly built vehicles will not be affected. In addition, the supplier introduced a new visual error-prevention mechanism to limit challenges like this going forward.

BYD mentioned the issue does not affect the vehicle’s handling or pose a safety risk during driving.

The company mentioned owners can take affected vehicles to their local service center for a free inspection and professional wheel rim replacement. It’s also offering a replacement vehicle or compensation for transportation expenses.

Effective immediately, BYD remarked, the warranty on affected Great Tang vehicles will also be restarted.

The Great Tang is on sale in China in pure electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains. The cheapest Premium EV variant starts at 239,900 yuan ($35,500).

Industry observers note that all versions use BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries. While the base Premium model uses a 105.79 kWh battery, the Flagship EV trim uses a larger 130.15 kWh battery that delivers up to 590 miles (950 km) of CLTC range. It starts at 269,900 yuan ($40,000).

The Great Tang is huge, measuring 5,263 mm long, 1,999 mm wide, and 1,800 mm high, with a wheelbase of 3,130 mm.

In comparison, that’s bigger than the Hyundai IONIQ 9 and Kia EV9. It’s closer in size to the Li Auto L9.

According to recent reports, based on a 1,000V architecture with BYD’s Flash Charging tech, the electric SUV can charge from 10% to 70% in five minutes. For a full recharge, or to go from 10% to 97%, it takes just nine minutes.

After launching in China, BYD executive vice president Stella Li said the flagship SUV will go on sale in Europe and other overseas markets by the end of 2026 or early 2027.

In a recent development, much of the bycatch in tropical fisheries is kept as "trash fish," which is processed into fishmeal, mainly for aquaculture feed. But this bycatch contains many juvenile fish, and there is concern that catching so many juveniles could lead to a decrease in the adult population. A new study led by researchers at Thailand's Department of Fisheries and Hokkaido University suggests that in these fisheries, the loss of juveniles might be partly offset by better survival among the remaining juveniles.

DOJ Moves to Forfeit $1.1 Billion in USDC Stolen in Binance Hack

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (671 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Justice Department filed to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC stolen from Binance by North Korean hackers, and Circle agreed to glitch replacement tokens.
  • The Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint Monday to take ownership of more than $1.1 billion in USDC that North Korean hackers stole from Binance last month, tokens that Circle froze but says it cannot move.
  • District Court for the District of Columbia, targets all USDC held at 36 addresses across 18 blockchains.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Justice Department filed to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC stolen from Binance by North Korean hackers, and Circle agreed to glitch replacement tokens.

The Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint Monday to take ownership of more than $1.1 billion in USDC that North Korean hackers stole from Binance last month, tokens that Circle froze but says it cannot move.

The complaint, filed in U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, targets all USDC held at 36 addresses across 18 blockchains. The department said the U.S. has now helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion in crypto from multiple sources since the Oct. 29 theft.

Recent findings suggest that on Nov. 12, the department mentioned it had court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion, out of a joint government and industry freeze of more than $2.7 billion. A temporary restraining order issued that day was served on Circle the same day.

Monday’s filing is the step that would let the government take title to the funds.

Recent findings suggest that circle blocked access to the USDC on or about Oct. 29, the complaint says. But the stablecoin issuer told prosecutors it does not have the technical ability to transfer the tokens out of the blocklisted addresses, which remain under the hackers’ control.

It has been revealed that instead, Circle has agreed to issue latest USDC equal to the frozen amount and send it to the U.S. once a court enters a forfeiture order. The complaint calls those tokens “Substitute USDC.”.

Industry observers note that several of the addresses are smart contract and hot wallet addresses on Binance’s own platform. The hackers took them over in the attack and drained some, but not all, of the funds before Circle stepped in, prosecutors wrote. “It appears Binance no longer controlled them,” the complaint claims.

According to recent reports, the filing also lays out how investigators say the breach began. A Binance employee contacted by a purported recruiter agreed to a job interview and was told to download software that contained malware, which matches what the exchange remarked earlier this month.

The infected device let the attackers plant an EIP-7702 injection. That feature, added to Ethereum in a 2025 upgrade, lets ordinary wallets temporarily act like smart contracts. Prosecutors mentioned the hackers used it to take control of Binance’s hot wallets and route funds to a “sweeper” contract that moved them out as soon as they arrived.

The first large transfer, about $780 million in USDC, left Binance on Ethereum at about 4:41 p.m. ET on Oct. 29, the complaint says. Another $43 million followed 18 minutes later. Investigators also traced AVAX that was split up, bridged and swapped until it became about $1.56 million in USDC.

Sources indicate that U.S. agencies attribute the theft to North Korean military hackers known as the Lazarus Group, or APT38. Investigators remarked some wallets that collected Binance funds also received money from the roughly $387 million Bitget hack in September, which the exchange’s CEO tied to North Korea.

The complaint also lists earlier heists it attributes to the group, including about $308 million from Japan’s DMM Bitcoin in May 2024 and about $1.5 billion from Bybit in February 2025.

“North Korean cyber hackers stole more than $6 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance, but swift coordination between the government and private sector partners helped prevent a substantial portion of those assets from disappearing,” mentioned Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Criminal Division.

Sources indicate that FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman stated North Korea “depends on sophisticated laundering techniques” to turn stolen crypto into money for the regime. The FBI, the Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation are handling the case.

“Secret Service investigators worked with precision to identify and freeze stolen funds within minutes of the hack,” remarked Special Agent in Charge Todd Bratz. “The criminals behind this intrusion believed they could outrun law enforcement, and they have been proven wrong.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have recorded their worst month since launching in January 2024, led by unprecedented withdrawals from BlackRock.
  • Data from Farside Investors indicates that the funds registered $569.69 million in net outflows on Nov.
  • Meanwhile, US spot Ethereum ETFs recorded $84.92 million in withdrawals on Monday, bringing their monthly outflows to $1.15 billion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have recorded their worst month since launching in January 2024, led by unprecedented withdrawals from BlackRock.

Data from Farside Investors indicates that the funds registered $569.69 million in net outflows on Nov. 23, pushing November's withdrawals to $4.71 billion. This surpasses the previous monthly record of $4.51 billion set in June by approximately $200 million.

Meanwhile, US spot Ethereum ETFs recorded $84.92 million in withdrawals on Monday, bringing their monthly outflows to $1.15 billion.

Together, the investment products have registered $5.86 billion in net withdrawals this month, reflecting deteriorating demand for crypto exposure through traditional financial markets.

The latest withdrawals came despite Monday's crypto market rally after Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's chief executive officer briefly lifted Bitcoin above $64,000. The top crypto has pared back these gains and is trading at $60.065 as of press time, per CryptoSlate's data.

Sources indicate that according to Farside Investors, BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) led Monday's withdrawals with $509.3 million, accounting for approximately 89% of the day's net outflows. Grayscale's Bitcoin Mini Trust and Bitwise's BITB followed with withdrawals of $61.08 million and $12.6 million, respectively.

Fidelity's FBTC was the only Bitcoin fund to attract fresh capital, registering $13.29 million in net inflows.

BlackRock has emerged as the epicenter of November's crypto ETF withdrawals, with IBIT recording nearly $4 billion in monthly net outflows, its highest since inception.

It has been revealed that the withdrawals represent approximately 85% of the combined outflows from US spot Bitcoin ETFs this month. IBIT has recorded withdrawals in 15 of November's 16 trading sessions.

Notably, the pace of redemptions has accelerated considerably over the past three trading sessions.

IBIT registered a then-record $541.1 million outflow on Nov. 19 before surpassing that figure with another $544.7 million in withdrawals on Nov. 20.

Combined with Monday's outflows, investors have pulled nearly $1.6 billion from the BlackRock fund over three consecutive trading sessions, representing about 40% of its monthly withdrawals.

Similar redemption pressure has extended to BlackRock's Ethereum investment products.

According to recent reports, according to Farside Investors, the asset manager's iShares Ethereum Trust (ETHA) registered $90.5 million in net outflows on Monday, bringing its monthly outflows to around $977 million. Notably, BlackRock’s staked Ether fund (ETHB) has also registered more than $90 million in outflows this month.

U.S. spot Bitcoin and Ether ETFs, November through Nov. 23, 2026.

BlackRock’s funds accounted for about 85% of Bitcoin ETF net outflows and 92% of Ether ETF net outflows.

In a recent development, november covers 16 trading sessions through Nov. 23, with four scheduled sessions still to come. Shares use each group’s net outflows as the denominator.

Sum Farside Investors’ daily net flows through Nov. 23. The BlackRock amounts are IBIT for Bitcoin and ETHA plus ETHB for Ether. Other funds equal the group total less those amounts. Bar widths show the magnitude of net outflows in U.S. dollars. Labels round to $0.01 billion and the nearest percentage point.

November covers 16 trading sessions through Nov. 23, with four scheduled sessions still to come. Shares use each group’s net outflows as the denominator.

Consequently, BlackRock's flagship Bitcoin and Ethereum funds have recorded about $4.9 billion in combined outflows this month.

Despite the recent redemptions, IBIT alone retains more than $62 billion in cumulative net inflows since its launch, while ETHA and ETHB hold over $10 billion in combined inflows.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, four trading sessions remain before November ends, including a shortened session on Nov. 27 following the Thanksgiving holiday.

With combined Bitcoin and Ethereum ETF withdrawals already approaching $6 billion, investors would need to reverse the prevailing redemption trend during the shortened trading week to prevent November's losses from deepening further.

Industry News: Perps and Swaps: How to Trade the News on Decrypt

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (713 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Decrypt

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Readers have traditionally learned about markets in one place and traded them in another.
  • Decrypt set out to close that gap in September 2026, when it announced The Information Exchange: a network that brings together news, data, market prices, probabilities and the ability to trade, around the subjects readers follow.
  • The Information Exchange sees Decrypt delivering both the reporting and the market infrastructure that links information to trading, while the Solana blockchain provides the network on which trades settle, including token swaps and perpetual futures.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Readers have traditionally learned about markets in one place and traded them in another. A story about Bitcoin, a public manufacturer or a commodity might shape a view, but acting on it meant opening an exchange or a trading app and starting over.

Decrypt set out to close that gap in September 2026, when it announced The Information Exchange: a network that brings together news, data, market prices, probabilities and the ability to trade, around the subjects readers follow.

The Information Exchange sees Decrypt delivering both the reporting and the market infrastructure that links information to trading, while the Solana blockchain provides the network on which trades settle, including token swaps and perpetual futures.

This guide explains what each one is and how to trade it on Decrypt.

Everything on The Information Exchange runs through a Decrypt Money Account, which rolled out on Solana in October 2026.

In a recent development, A Money Account holds one balance that funds every product on Decrypt: swaps, perpetual futures and prediction markets.The account is self-custodial, meaning Decrypt does not hold consumers' private keys and cannot act on their behalf. It is designed to work without seed phrases, and network fees are covered, so users don't need to hold SOL, Solana's native token, to pay for transactions.

It has been revealed that in November 2026, Decrypt added confidential transfers, using Solana Privacy Rings from infrastructure firm Helius. Users can send funds without the amounts appearing on Solana's public ledger, and can switch the feature on by selecting "Enable" on the Private Balance panel of the Portfolio page. As of November 2026, privacy applies to transfers only, not to swaps or prediction market positions.

Solana Privacy Rings use zero-knowledge proofs, which let owners prove they own and can spend a balance without revealing how much it holds.

A swap exchanges one token for another at the current market price. Instead of placing an order on an exchange and waiting for it to fill, the trader sends one token and receives another in a single transaction.

In a recent development, swaps on Decrypt are powered by Jupiter, a Solana trading platform that offers swaps, lending, borrowing, perpetual futures and portfolio tools. Jupiter finds prices across Solana's trading venues, so users don't need to choose where a trade is executed.

At time of publication, swaps cover a select group of major cryptocurrencies and Solana tokens, as well as tokenized stocks, commodities and other real-world assets.

As of November 2026, the Assets panel of the Portfolio page groups holdings into crypto, stocks, commodities and collectibles, and lists tokens including SOL, BTC, ETH, XRP and HYPE.

In a recent development, perpetual futures, or perps, are contracts that let traders bet on whether an asset's price will rise or fall without owning the asset. Unlike traditional futures, they have no expiry date. A trader who expects the price to rise goes "long," and one who expects it to fall goes "short.".

It has been revealed that perps are usually traded with leverage, which lets a trader control a larger position than their deposit would otherwise allow. Leverage magnifies gains and losses alike, and if the market moves against a position far enough, it can be liquidated, or closed automatically, wiping out the trader's margin.

Perps on Decrypt are powered by Phoenix, a fully onchain perpetuals exchange on Solana developed by Ellipsis Labs—making Decrypt the first media platform to offer perps trading alongside its journalism.

Recent findings suggest that as of November 2026, Phoenix offers more than 100 perps markets on Decrypt, covering crypto, U.S. stocks, gold and pre-IPO companies. Markets trade around the clock, with leverage of up to 40x, according to Phoenix.

Decrypt looks to keep adding products to The Information Exchange, including Situation Rooms: pages that combine breaking news, live data, prices, probabilities and trading around a single subject.

Decrypt operates The Information Exchange, Decrypt Money Accounts and the swaps, perpetual futures and prediction market products described in this guide.

It has been revealed that perpetual futures are leveraged products and carry a high risk of loss. Availability may vary by region. Nothing in this guide is investment advice.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kia became the first non-European brand to score a hat trick at the 2026 Golden Steering Wheel Awards, Germany’s most prestigious auto awards.

The Korean automaker won a triple crown at the 2026 Golden Steering Wheel Awards, with the EV2, K4 Sportswagon, and EV5 taking first in their class.

This is the first time a non-European brand has won three Golden Steering Wheel Awards in a single year in the prestigious award’s 50-year history.

In a recent development, the award is organized by AUTO BILD and BILD am SONNTAG with 90 new models nominated this year. Readers chose 27 finalists, three in each of the nine classes, which were then tested by a panel of celebrities and auto experts.

The judges tested the vehicles at the DEKRA-Lausitzring racetrack. Vehicles were judged on handling, comfort, ease of use, quality, and everyday practicality, as well as the sustainability and value they offer.

Kia won across three very different categories with the fully electric EV2 and EV5, alongside the gas-powered K4 Sportswagon.

The EV2, Kia’s entry-level electric SUV, won the award for the “Best Car Under €30,000.” Developed specifically for Europe, the compact EV is only 4.06 meters long, but offers up to 403 liters of cargo space.

It also offers a WLTP driving range of up to 453 km (281 miles), which is among the longest in its class.

Recent findings suggest that kia’s EV5 beat out the Audi Q3 and Cupra Formentor VZ5 in the compact SUV category. Launched in December, the EV5 is about the size of the Sportage.

Recent findings suggest that it’s available with front- and all-wheel-drive powertrains and offers a range of over 550 km (341 miles). Depending on the configuration, the EV5 can tow up to 1,800 kg (about 4,000 lbs).

Lastly, the Kia K4 Sportswagon, debuted in May, outperformed the newly introduced Volkswagen ID.3 Neo and Cupra Born in the compact class.

In Europe, Kia offers a full lineup of all-electric vehicles, from the entry-level EV2 to the EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, three-row EV9, and PV5 van.

Sadly, Kia has no aims to sell the EV2 or EV5 in the US, but its popular EV3 (see our review) is now available. In 2024, the Kia EV3 won the Golden Steering Wheel award for “Best Car under €40,000.”.

Sources indicate that the 2027 Kia EV3 starts at $29,890, making it among the most affordable EVs in the US. It’s available in five trims and two battery packs.

The base Kia EV3 Light has a 58.3 kWh battery that provides up to 221 miles of range, while the Wind, Land, GT-Line, and GT use an 81.4 kWh battery for up to 321 miles of range.

Tech Report: South Korea Unveils Crypto Bill Capping Exchange Ownership at 20%

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (698 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • South Korea’s Financial Services Commission on Tuesday unveiled a government bill that would cap a major shareholder’s stake in a crypto exchange at 20%, open the door to domestic coin offerings and let bank-led groups matter won stablecoins.
  • The draft, titled the Act on the Innovation of the Digital Asset Industry and Protection of Users, was presented at a Virtual Asset Committee meeting chaired by FSC Chairman Lee Eog-weon.
  • Lee noted the law would raise trust and transparency in Korea’s digital asset market and help draw new money into the industry.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

South Korea’s Financial Services Commission on Tuesday unveiled a government bill that would cap a major shareholder’s stake in a crypto exchange at 20%, open the door to domestic coin offerings and let bank-led groups matter won stablecoins.

The draft, titled the Act on the Innovation of the Digital Asset Industry and Protection of Users, was presented at a Virtual Asset Committee meeting chaired by FSC Chairman Lee Eog-weon. It would replace Korea’s two-track system, built on an anti-money-laundering law and a 2024 user protection act, with a single framework covering the industry, markets and users.

Lee noted the law would raise trust and transparency in Korea’s digital asset market and help draw new money into the industry. He said the government would do everything it can to see the bill fully debated in the National Assembly and enacted promptly.

Sources indicate that under the bill, exchanges would become “digital asset platform operators,” a designation reserved for firms that hold separate licenses for dealing, brokerage and custody. The FSC modeled the ownership limit on the rules for alternative trading systems in the stock market.

Major shareholders could own up to 20%, or up to 34% with FSC approval under a presidential decree. Shares above the limit would lose their voting rights. Existing exchanges would get three years after designation to comply, and small and midsize exchanges could get up to three more.

Recent findings suggest that the cap could reach some of Korea’s best-known exchanges. Mirae Asset Consulting owns 97.15% of Digital X, the exchange formerly known as Korbit, The Korea Herald reported. Naver Financial’s planned share-swap takeover of Dunamu, the operator of Upbit, would make the exchange a wholly owned subsidiary.

The FSC declined to comment on specific companies, the paper said.

“Ownership restrictions are necessary to strengthen exchanges’ public accountability and neutrality,” Yoo Young-jun, director general of the FSC’s Digital Financial Policy Bureau, remarked at a briefing, citing more than 10 million exchange accounts in Korea.

Industry observers note that the bill would also move trade execution, listing reviews and market surveillance from self-regulation to formal rules. Exchanges would need outside directors to make up a majority of their boards, plus audit committees and compliance officers.

Sources indicate that domestic initial coin offerings would be allowed as long as issuers file a white paper with the FSC before marketing tokens to the public. The release pointed to a platform manufacturer that sidestepped Korea’s ICO ban by setting up a foundation abroad, then sold its token through local exchanges. Exchanges would have to file and publish a report on each token they list.

Industry observers note that stablecoins, called digital payment tokens in the bill, could only be issued by licensed firms with at least 5 billion won in capital. At first, the FSC intends to allow issuance only by consortiums in which banks hold a majority stake, though fintech and tech companies could be the largest single shareholder.

Recent findings suggest that issuers would have to hold reserves of at least 100% of tokens outstanding at banks or similar institutions, and they could not pay holders interest. Tokens with more than 1 trillion won outstanding could be designated as significant, and the Bank of Korea could request joint inspections of their issuers.

Sources indicate that licensed firms would carry no-fault liability to customers for hacks and system outages. The FSC could impose punitive fines of up to 10% of revenue when a security lapse causes an incident. The release cited a November 2025 theft from one exchange’s wallet and an October 2026 hack at another, without naming either.

Industry observers note that insider-trading bans would extend to former employees for a year after they leave. The FSC could also freeze accounts when there is substantial suspicion of unfair trading. Regulators have already shown a willingness to punish exchanges, having fined Bithumb $24.6 million and suspended its fresh-user services for six months over anti-money-laundering violations in March.

According to recent reports, last week, the FSC was reported to be preparing guidelines that would let about 3,500 listed companies and professional-investor firms buy bitcoin. The newly introduced bill now heads to the National Assembly.

Bitcoin reclaimed $60,000 on Tuesday after a volatile 24 hours that saw its price swing by more than $5,000.

Data from CryptoSlate indicated that the flagship digital asset recovered to $60,087 as of press time after falling to as low as $59,322, surrendering most of the gains from Monday's rally above $64,000 following Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's chief executive officer.

In a recent development, the Kobeissi Letter noted that the AI firm's shares had declined approximately 28% from their post-IPO high. The stock touched $81.28 in Tuesday's premarket trading, down about 29% from its debut-day peak of $115.10.

Four Tuesday observations show the dip and rebound around each market’s benchmark.

By the later quotes, both markets were back above their respective thresholds.

The early Bitcoin time is a report timestamp. ANT observations are extended-hours trades and the final Bitcoin quote is for Coinbase. The marked observations cannot establish first crossings or causation.

Report and market timestamps are shown in Eastern time, rounded to the displayed minute. The gap is 6:14 a.m. minus 12:56 a.m. Bitcoin’s later quote is rounded to the nearest dollar. Desktop markers are spaced by elapsed time. Mobile lists events in order with spacing for readability.

While Nvidia shares surged nearly 30% during Monday's broader market rally, Anthropic closed 1.4% lower at $87.64, extending its post-IPO decline.

Europe’s electric car sales jump 49% as global EV sales grow

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Global EV sales climbed 8% in October, with Europe’s battery electric vehicle (BEV) sales jumping 49% and North America posting its first year-over-year increase in 2026.
  • Recent findings suggest that drivers bought 2.09 million EVs worldwide last month, according to latest data from Benchmark Mineral Intelligence.
  • Benchmark’s figures include both BEVs and plug-in hybrids (PHEVs) in the passenger-car and light-duty vehicle markets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Global EV sales climbed 8% in October, with Europe’s battery electric vehicle (BEV) sales jumping 49% and North America posting its first year-over-year increase in 2026. But that North American rebound comes with a big catch.

Recent findings suggest that drivers bought 2.09 million EVs worldwide last month, according to latest data from Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. That’s down 3% from September, but it brings sales for the first 10 months of 2026 to 17.5 million – up 5% from the same period last year.

Benchmark’s figures include both BEVs and plug-in hybrids (PHEVs) in the passenger-car and light-duty vehicle markets.

Europe sold 510,000 EVs in October, up 36% year over year. Fully electric cars did most of the work: BEV sales rose 49%, while plug-in hybrids grew 7%.

According to recent reports, that puts October’s growth ahead of Europe’s 31% increase for the year so far. The region has now sold 4.5 million EVs in 2026.

Sources indicate that sales fell 17% from September’s record, but September got a boost from the UK’s twice-yearly registration plate change. The year-over-year figures give a clearer view of how quickly the market is growing.

Germany’s EV share topped 45% of new car sales, its highest level since December 2022. That earlier peak came as buyers rushed to get cars before subsidy cuts took effect. Fully electric car sales in Germany rose almost 80% from a year earlier to more than 95,000.

In a recent development, UK EV sales increased 30%. That’s particularly notable because the Electric Car Grant was already available in October 2025, although fewer models qualified then. So this growth comes against a market that was already getting government support.

And in Portugal, EVs accounted for 55% of new car sales in October, following a sharp rise in their market share over the past few months.

North American EV sales rose 24% year over year to 130,000 in October, the region’s first annual increase of 2026. Sales were flat from September, while the year-to-date decline narrowed to 21%, from 24% a month earlier. The region has sold 1.3 million EVs so far this year.

US EV sales reached around 110,000 units in October.

But here’s the catch: October 2025 was the first month after the federal EV tax credit expired. The credit ended for vehicles acquired after September 30, 2025, and sales dropped sharply afterward.

In a recent development, october 2026 is therefore being compared with a month when sales plummeted. A positive annual number doesn’t mean US demand has returned to its pre-expiration level.

“October is the first month compared against a period without the US federal tax credit, and the US market has stabilized at a lower level rather than recovered,” stated Charles Lester, Benchmark’s data manager.

The flat month-over-month figure helps tell that story: Sales have steadied, but the market is operating from a lower base.

Sources indicate that china sold 1.14 million EVs in October, up 5% from September but down 12% year over year. That annual decline was smaller than September’s 18% drop.

Sales through October reached 9.1 million, down 11%, compared with a 13% year-to-date decline at the end of September.

In a recent development, even with fewer EVs being sold, their share of China’s latest car market reached a fresh high. That’s because the wider passenger car market is shrinking faster.

According to recent reports, chinese automakers are continuing to produce vehicles and look overseas for buyers. Passenger car exports of fresh energy vehicles – China’s category covering BEVs and PHEVs – reached nearly 600,000 in October. That’s another monthly record, up from 558,000 in September.

Those exports face more pressure ahead. The EU has agreed to cap imports of Chinese-built hybrids, and China will reduce its EV export VAT rebate from 13% to 9% starting April 1, 2027.

Recent findings suggest that outside China, Europe, and North America, EV sales rose 85% year over year to 300,000 in October. Those markets have bought 2.6 million EVs so far in 2026, up 93%.

Australia’s sales jumped more than 200% in October, and EVs have gained market share sharply this year. But that hasn’t translated into healthy dealer profits, according to Benchmark. More brands, many of them Chinese, are competing for buyers, spreading sales across more companies and squeezing dealer margins.

In a recent development, brazil’s growth has also been huge, although Benchmark cautions that some of its drivers are temporary. Importers brought vehicles in ahead of phased tariff increases, a fuel crisis pushed more buyers toward EVs, and BYD increased production at its Brazilian factory.

In a recent development, nothing like consumer economics to drive sales. Local story about consumer economics: Windturbines on land is not popular. However, the locals realised they could heat their home for $300/year (in Denmark(!)) with these wind turbines and then they were tolerated! Same with cars - people gravitate to cheaper alternatives despite the more frequent charging and initial higher prices.

Industry observers note that as the tariff increases take full effect and fuel price pressure eases, Benchmark expects those boosts to fade. BYD’s local production, which will also supply Argentina and Mexico, is set to become the main remaining support for that growth.

UniCredit Opens Bitcoin to Italian Savers, Capping Gains at 65%
